Actually CK2 at its core is a good game. I played hundreds of hours offline and own most of the major DLC. But my gripe with this game is the poor quality of the recent DLC (and associated patches), each of them introducing (partly game-breaking) bugs and/or unfinished features which are hardly dealt with or not at all.
Examples includes the Decadence system introduces in one of the first DLC (Sword of Islam) which was not working as intended for (3?) years or the Converter for EU4 which was sold long time even it was known to be not functional . While the first few DLC are quite nice or at least ok, the quality of recent releases rapidly dropped i think with "Rajas of India", then "Charlemagne" and finally "Way of Life".
The latter one is just the most recent example of bad practise: Released just few days before Christmas "Way of Life" just not delivered poorly balanced features (e.g. insanely overpowered intrigue or seduction) but also introduced the so called "dismiss levies bug" which rendered the AI unable to declare war not only for the owners of the DLC but also for everyone else(due to patch)! That's a borderline rip-off considering that most people cannot play the game during the holidays until the developers choose to come back from their own around 6th of January.
EDIT: A patch was released which solved the levies bug and other major issues on 17th of January 2015.  Still, the bug forums are full and a lot of glaring issues remain untouched.  While admittely these bugs are minor compared to the levies bug, overall they are a serious annoyance (e.g. undisposable anti-popes and continous religious unrest) and the game is faaaaaar away from beeing stable or polished!
This is especially outrageous as a few days (Feb.2015) ago a total of 3 new DLCs for 2015 have been announced BUT the patches which should fix the old bugs have been tied to those patches. SO as the next DLC has not been announced in detail we are looking forward to even more months in which the game remains broken on so many levels!
TLDR: This is a negative response to Paradox bad practise of  constantly releasing hardly polished DLCs which introduce new (partly game breaking) bugs and/or features instead of addressing these issues! This full-price game (albeit costing 150 EUR with all DLCs and already about 3 years old) has become something that plays like a bug-ridden EARLY ACCESS title or BETA with many features not yet working as intended!

It is a twin-stick shooter really like Nuclear Throne, but with RPG elements: you can loot many items, customize your armors, upgrade weapons and stuff. Stats (such as speed, HP, regen...) are visible and countable.
There is the EP system : every moves (shoot, dash, melee attack, etc) cost EP point which regen fasts but once all gone, you have to wait to recharge your system. This thing prevents blind spamming. The terrain is also a game changer with different things like ice & conveyor belt which influence your movements : it is good.
The game is really fast paced with the presence of skills like dash, the speed of bullets, the celerity of melee attacks, the responding animation... You can choose between 3 classes with their own unique ability and 20+ skills to begin with (passive or active). Pixel art is very nice and music too.
The problem is see with this game is the so-so break at the end of every level, when you have to analyse your loot, recycle, upgrade, etc. It is pleasing but it breaks the pace and during that phase, the controls are tedious imo.
It is less "jump in & play" than Nuclear Throne, games lasts longer I believe, and I think that's the weak spot of the game. I'm interested to see how the game will become in the future.
Another problem is the loot : it is very cool, we loot many items, but in-game we pick up things but we don't really know what it is, and at the end of the level I feel flooded with so many items. But this feeling is only something of the singleplayer, because in multiplayer you spend time to trade/share items. And btw, I think the real game begins when you play in co-op.

Casual hilarity and an extremely deep combat system. 4 classes with a wide variety of weapons with unique attack animations. With this game you have an unprecedented amount of control over what side or direction you're attacking from, or how fast or slow the attack will be. By dragging your mouse into your strikes you will hit sooner. By dragging away you can delay your attack and induce a block in order to leave them open. This game features an extremely amusing chat tree system which is as useful for telling your duel opponent he smells like a woman as it is for informing your teammate someone is behind him. A quirky dry Monty Python like chatter is often cut off mid sentence by blood curdling screaming. This game is very casual unless you want to play the Duel game type but I would not recommend it because it lends itself to a lot of very underhanded and lame play styles and toxic players. My favorite gamemode is one that is rare to see nowadays but it is called "Classic duel" which was created by the community before the official Duel mode was released. In classic duels the players will only engadge in "honorable" duels in which both players agree to foght by either bowing or war crying at one another. Enforcement against dishonorable duels or "randoming" is enforced by group ganking of the offender and or kicking. The fact that something like this even exists at all is a testament to the community in itself, not to say that toxic players have never ruined the experience. If a giant cluster F*** is more your style try out FFA. If you want an element of team work try Last Team Standing or TDM. Buy this if you love intense point of view melee combat and quirky game atmosphere that is both casual and has a very high skill ceiling.

My stance on free games is they all get a positive rec unless they're not even worth your time. This game has some issues but it's mostly fun for the 3-4 hours you'll spend with it. It's a "collect all the endings" type of RPG set in a single classroom where you have to figure out how to confess your love to a girl. You will have to do some very minor puzzle solving to progress but it's more about just doing all the things since each thing leads to a different ending.
On the minus side, the translation is far below professional quality. It's Google Translate quality. It's still entirely comprehensible, though. It's also done in the typical Japanese indie arcade game style where the game runs in a very low resolution window with no options for scaling, audio levels, control configs, etc. You can Alt+Enter to make it fullscreen and that's about it.
The other issue is a minor spoiler and relates to unlocking the last 5 endings. To avoid SOME frustration, continue reading: After you unlock all of the items and endings up to collecting the item in the locked cabinet, there is a very specific sequence you need to follow to unlock the last part of the game. You need to collect the item in the cabinet, get Julie to leave, close the curtains and then while the timer says 3, you have to confess. Even if you do all of that, there's only like a 1 out of 3 chance you'll progress to the next part which allows you to get the last 5 endings so, like I said, that will only save you SOME frustration. If it doesn't work, just keep doing the sequence until it does.
Overall, not a bad way to spend a few hours. With a proper translation, it would even be worth a few bucks.

Hmm... how do I put this? Glass Wing was a rather interesting game. I found out about this game awhile back when I was watching a podcast with DrWolf001 and he mentioned playing the voice of the antagonist Ferace. Was debating whether or not to get it, and decided to get it in the end.
Before I get into the review, I strongly recommend to play this with a controller. I used a Dualshock 3 controller to play this and it worked perfectly.
Like I mentioned earlier, this game was rather interesting. You play the role of the Glass Wing Mayfly who is trying to get away from the demon Ferace, after he attempts to capture you. During the course of the game, you find various tools as well as unlock new abilities in order to progress through each map. The game is composed of several maps with puzzles as well as platforming stages.
One of the interesting concepts I found while playing is the use of tools and the "combat". The game strongly advises against fighting the monsters that roam around the game (The game description mentions Mayfly being very weak and not suited for combat) thus the tools you find around the game are instead used for exploring. Each tool has a purpose for getting around (this includes using a scythe to cut down plants, a sword for cutting thorns, a hammer for smashing certain blocks, etc.)
The music in this game was actually really nice to listen to. I actually recognized a few of them as several of the tracks used are from the artist Makkon, an artist who once did pony music (A Waltz for Trixie and Hallowed Waltz being the two used that I recognized).
One of the main gripes I had while playing this game was surprisingly not the controls, but the platforming levels (or Twilight Trials as they're called). I got through the first Twilight Trial perfectly fine, but aftwards they just got really painful to do. These levels were rather punishing if you fall off because you would have to start all the way back at the beginning. (This really isn't too horrible, but it gives me nostalgic moments of when I played games like Super Mario Sunshine and having to play those FLUDD-less platforming levels)
Another minor gripe I had involved the final segment of the game. There is a glitch that causes Mayfly to fall through the map should you die and try to reload the file. This was fixed by simply closing out of the game and reloading the save. Minor, but really annoying.
Overall, I thought this game was a mixture of interesting and frustration. I enjoyed the interactions with Mayfly and Ferace and I rather enjoyed solving the puzzles (I'm still surprised I managed to beat this without consulting a guide... actually I couldn't find a guide for this game. Might write one up in the future if I feel like playing through again.) Would I recommend this game to anyone? Maybe... Maybe not... Depends on one's patience threshold as this game rather tested mine at some points, but it was rather satisfying when I managed to get past said points.

This is a beautifully flawed game; similar to a pilot episode of a TV show, this is one of those things that's kinda rough right now has tons of potential to be incredible in the future. The concept of a ghost possession-based murder mystery game is really cool, in my personal opinion. If you're a big fan of Danny Phantom, this is a dream come true. It's a very short game and there were some iffy segments, but overall the gameplay was very creative and fairly well-done. Looks good, even when running on a toaster. This is a very story-driven game, but this is an exception of my regular view that having a story in a video game is like watching porn for plot; the story is crucial to the murder mystery based gameplay.
Some things that irked me:
-There were parts where you could kind of tell that the devs put in obstacles because they needed something to fill up the playtime.
-There's no new game plus or option to go back and finish getting the collectibles, that are kind of... there, and feel a bit tacked on, after going into the final boss fight.
Overall, I'd probably give it a 7/10 in its current state, but I think a sequel could EASILY be a 9/10 if the devs take advantage of their strong points and get the budget to make another. Go back and watch the pilot episode of your favorite TV show and then the most recent one, and you'll see what I mean. Although it's rough around the edges, the concept is definitely there and has LOADS of potential to be great. Right now it's $15, but if you can find it on sale, it's definitely worth picking up.
If you like oldschool shooting games like Quake 2 or Serious Sam, then you can't miss Hard Reset!

'Hand of Fate' is a wonderful game.
It's a fascinating blend of card deck builder and adventure game, with a dash of philosophical introspection. One of the things I particularly like about it is that it teaches you how to play as you go, you don't need a lot of preparation before setting off on your first adventure. There aren't many controls to learn, and the mechanics are introduced naturally along the way.
It's a 'roguelike'; you only have one life -- but death, when it does come, isn't much of a drawback, since you retain any cards you gain in every session, for use in the next 'life'. Even when you lose, you win.
The artwork is superb, as is the background music. The dealer's voice is particularly well done. (It sounds to me like Jeremy Irons, but the credits say it's Anthony Skordi.)
The only real criticism I have of it is that I find the fight scenes a bit awkward due to the choice of a fixed camera angle. I'm spending far too much time mashing buttons in the fight scenes as left becomes right and up becomes down, and I fear for my keyboard!
It's only single player (I don't mind that at all, though I know it's a turn-off for many).
I picked it up on sale, but would happily have paid full price for it (why are such gems so few and far between?)
10/10 would delete my memory for play this master piece again.

In a lot of RPGs you play the hero that must save the world. But heroes are not alone; they need to find friends to fight with and shops to buy weapons, armor and healing items. This game dares to ask "what if you were the NPC standing behind the desk in the item shops?"
Yes, you read that right, in Recettear you play as Recette Lemongrass, the cute loli who runs an item shop to repay her father’s gigantic debt. So if you're looking for a big adventure you might want to look somewhere else, but if you're looking for a good administration game then you've come to the right place. Even though it's labeled as an RPG, Recettear is mostly a strategy game: you must know what to buy, what to sell, at what price, when to open your shop, when to buy items and when to go to dungeons. You must do everything to make sure you can pay the required amount of your father's debt by the end of the week. As you level up, you unlock new abilities such as taking orders, fusing items, customizing and expanding your store, so you won't be doing the same all over and over.
In general, Recettear offers a very plant experience and a good challenge; however it does have a few downsides. First of all, the dungeons despite being randomized will feel very repetitive after a while: in every floor you will be running in endless narrow corridors and square rooms, making the enemies and the layout (which are also repeated several times) the only variation. The postgame doesn't have much to offer either, aside from the survival and + modes all you will get is a 100 floor dungeon that continues the story but introduces no new enemies or layouts and a 30 floor dungeon where you'll be dead before you notice even if your adventurer is level 99 (but hey, at least the later offers a bit of challenge). After you clear the main quest you don't need to pay any more debts so running your shop, which is the main aspect of the game, becomes pointless.
In summary: despite the dungeon system not being the best, the shop managing is really well done and anyone who enjoys administration games should try Recettear.

Have played this Korean gem MMO on its own client for quite some time. Not overly, yet just as much as a connoisseur like me would want to, enough for shaping an opinion.
Sure, the company managing it isn't probably doing the best job handling clients/players, also in keeping the game clean from bots and whatnot. Yet I'll not take that too much into account, as I will more try to reflect on what the game itself offers.
The Koreans have indeed made a wonderful effort here - the game-world is beautiful, so are the models and graphics, the landscape and details. Even the music and the narration are very compelling - I also love the elvish-sounding Korean-speaking NPCs here and there. English ones are awful though, text would have been enough of a translation (would really like the option that I'd get to go full-out Korean mode and change audio language entirely - Asian voice actors are overall and usually far better for games and the like, with voice-acting schools far exceeding the West's).
As for gameplay, it does get somewhat repetitive, yet the environments and open-world feeling make up for it. I also love the risk and freedom that trade runs and piracy offer. Kinda reminds me of me ol' runescape days, stalking the wilderness. Classes are also varied, and so are the options for character builds. Even though I'd prefer even more of that - Diablo 2 style - it's quite a meaty system here as well, in comparison to others on the market. Crafting in-game is rather significant here, as it should be in an in-depth MMO.
Overall, I love the game for its aesthetics, and really do enjoy the fluidity and varied nature of the whole experience. This makes ArcheAge my favorite MMO aside Guild Wars 2, Mortal Online and Secret World.
As a game, I'd score this 7/10 - I'm not all that huge on MMOs. :)

One of the more fun FPS games I've played in a while. A little rough around the edges, but very good overall. It will let you get a bead on the combat situation before it's in your face. Without a doubt, if you are a fan of old school first person shooters, Hard Reset will hit you right in the nostalgia. Side-scrolling galore, straight-up bullet storms (no pun intended), and huge, monsterous bosses. The game has an awesome sci-fi/dystopian set piece. And man - this game is challenging. You are often pitted against an army of robots in corriders - relegating strafing to mere slamming against walls.
Despite the strong points of the game, I feel that the makers did not adequately fill the environment. Enemy-types are sparse despite the add-on: You basically face (1) two-legged robots with 3 variations, (2) foot soldier robots with 3 variations, and (3) two "gorilla-type" robots with two variations. There is no variety of weapons per say, but rather weapon-alternative fires. The greatest downfall of this game is the story: Despite googling it and reading the message boards, it appears no one has a firm grasp of what is going on. Comic-esque cut scenes do their best to present something that resembles a plot but fall short of cohesiveness.
I am really on the wall about whether or not I would recommend this game. If you are inclined towards old school FPS's, get it. If you fall in to lulls really quick due to repetitive enemy types and an abscence of a story , I'd avoid this game.

The game also teases you with openings beneath fences etc, but the lack of a crouch or pick up ability serve to frustrate. Similarly, jumping is flawed... you cannot jump over balustrades or ledges that you might otherwise expect to, instead our action hero has to walk to the stairs.... You spend a lot of time fighting multiple enemies at once, but their surprise appearances are entirely predictable. The art style is quite nice and the engine smooth, but the levels are all pretty samey and it gets tired quickly. There also seem to be a lot of fork lift trucks blocking the way, hardly puzzling, and the game quite frequently tells you where to go with a hint system before you even have a chance to figure it out (if indeed you could). So in summary, it's an ok game, but not really recommended. It pains me to say that I can't really recommend this game.  It is the best-looking retro-pixel game I have ever played. Every pixel has been painstaking placed, every animation brilliantly detailed and expressive.  But somewhere in those 10 years of development they forgot to check if their game was fun.
Maybe its because we've had 10 years of innovation in this market, or maybe I'm just spoiled; owlboy can't really compare to Shovel Knight or Axiom Verge.  Switching out friends to change weapons is gimmicky, moving across the map is trivial.  Controls aren't particularly tight.  Once you start there is not much depth or ramp-up in difficultly as you proceed.  It seems like there is a good story hiding in here but you can only really guess at it even after gathering all the lore collectables and such.
Worth picking up if on sale, but as a whole, I'm pretty disappointed in this.  If you're looking for a light-hearted easy game to breeze through, this is a good choice.  Was a good length for this kind of game, but by the end I was bored enough with the main game loop that I was ready for it to be over.
I'd recommend this game. I'd also recommend you playing it with friends, since it's much more enjoyable that way. It's a bit buggy and rough around the edges, but all in all a good game.

Following on from its extraordinary predecessor (Mass Effect), the second title in the blockbuster series offers another phenomonal story with fantastic gameplay to go along with it! It is a major step up from the first game in many aspects, such as the character development, gameplay, and graphics. Additionally, any decisions you may have made in the first game can be carried over to have effect in Mass Effect 2.
Gameplay-wise, ME2 is a third-person shooter with RPG elements. The combat mechanics are solid, giving you the ability to choose from a variety of classes and skills of which you can level up to make your character more powerful. You are also given the ability to command a small squad to help you in your fight against the enemy. Over the course of the game you can recruit new members to your team, completing quests in order to do so. This can even lead to gaining loyalty from said teammates through additional quests to unlock more skills for them. Aside from that, there are a lot of choices to be made when in dialogue sequences in the game that can change how certain people perceive you, adding to the immersion.
Graphics and sound wise, the game is superb. The art direction is brilliant and really creates a beautiful game world for you to explore. There are many planets you can travel to and many aliens to encounter on the planets. Whilst the pre-rendered cutscenes can take away from the excellence of the in-game graphics, it is overall quite a flashy game that still looks great on lower graphics settings. Which leads on to performance - this game runs great even on low-mid range computers!
So, overall, Mass Effect 2 is of current my favourite game. The immersive world, fantastic gameplay, and blockbuster story will make you love it too! I can definitely recommend this to fans of third-person shooters and RPGs.
Enjoy! :D

In the passing years since I’ve started writing about games, I have been loathe to refer to any of them as “charming”. It just feels like a cop-out adjective: something that could very easily be applied to any number of indie games that put a heavy focus on character, story, and a friendly or sometimes melancholy atmosphere. There have been a ton of clever, inviting indie games that have been released in the past decade, and an endless stream of them could use that forbidden adjective. Shovel Knight, Firewatch, Minecraft, Spelunky: the list goes on and on. “Charming” just sounds simultaneously lazy and condescending, and I’ve tried to avoid it.
But here today, I am forced to use that word when it comes to Owlboy. Because no other word encapsulates the feeling I get from D-Pad Studios’ indie platformer better than that troublesome little moniker, so let’s just get right into it, shall we?
Owlboy is charming.

I have a mixed bag of emotions regarding this game.
At its core, the game is amazing.  You pick one of three classes, and throughout the game you can equip hardware.  The weapons are all very creative and variable, and always feel unique.  At the end of each level, you choose your next environment.  There are boss battles and many crazy enemies.  The theme and atmosphere is amazing here.  I can also guarantee that this is one of the best soundtracks in a game I've played.
There isn't actually all that much to the game as a whole.
On the negative end, the game sometimes feels long and tedious.  considering you can die on any moment's notice, the levels sometimes feel frustratingly drawn out.  Also, there is little "feel" to when you are about to die.  This game is very difficult, yes, but if I die thinking my health was fine (there is a health bar, but very little "impact" when you are hit, and the health bar is easy to ignore).
In its current state, I'm on the fence as to what review to give it.  The game is very fun and EXTREMELY cool, but a lot of the game can feel like a frustrating pain in the @$$.
Here is what I consider a deal-maker though: The developers, Flying Oak Games, are amazing.  They update the game almost weekly, and every single update feels extremely productive.  When I bought this game a few months ago, I hated it.  It felt bland and lots of the content felt arbitrary.  Now, almost all of my previous gripes are gone.  There is even an in-game option to send the developers feedback.
You could argue that I'm saying the game "has potential," but I'd say it's different- I'm extremel confident that this game will someday be a shining gem amongst a sea of turds.  And that being said, the game isn't even bad.  It's still a lot of fun in its current state.
I'd say that if the trailer appeals to you, and the 10$ price isn't unnattractive, then you should go for it.

Casual hilarity and an extremely deep combat system. 4 classes with a wide variety of weapons with unique attack animations. With this game you have an unprecedented amount of control over what side or direction you're attacking from, or how fast or slow the attack will be. By dragging your mouse into your strikes you will hit sooner. By dragging away you can delay your attack and induce a block in order to leave them open. This game features an extremely amusing chat tree system which is as useful for telling your duel opponent he smells like a woman as it is for informing your teammate someone is behind him. A quirky dry Monty Python like chatter is often cut off mid sentence by blood curdling screaming. This game is very casual unless you want to play the Duel game type but I would not recommend it because it lends itself to a lot of very underhanded and lame play styles and toxic players. My favorite gamemode is one that is rare to see nowadays but it is called "Classic duel" which was created by the community before the official Duel mode was released. In classic duels the players will only engadge in "honorable" duels in which both players agree to foght by either bowing or war crying at one another. Enforcement against dishonorable duels or "randoming" is enforced by group ganking of the offender and or kicking. The fact that something like this even exists at all is a testament to the community in itself, not to say that toxic players have never ruined the experience. If a giant cluster F*** is more your style try out FFA. If you want an element of team work try Last Team Standing or TDM. Buy this if you love intense point of view melee combat and quirky game atmosphere that is both casual and has a very high skill ceiling.

Ya know I've probably only gotten halfway through the game but I have waayyyy too many complaints than pluses.
I played ME1 and I thoroughly enjoyed it even though I was rushing through it to get to ME2 since I heard it was the best in the series.
Could it have been over hyped? For me, it's all about the games content and how it is presented to me not how "hyped" a game is. I don't care how much you try to sell me your product a good game doesn't have to sell me the product they only need to present it and well ME2 fails on a lot of levels.
First are the controls. Imagine you were playing game and you learned the controls there. Now the next game of that series is released but the controls are different and it feels wonky and out of place. That's exactly how it feels here. I prefer the controls of ME1 over ME2 and I still would even if I didn't play ME1. I'm going to sound like a broken record when I say this but I'm going to be saying this a hell of a lot here, if something ain't broke then don't fix  it.
Secondly the game play. Pretty sure any gamer would rather have weapons use HEAT over ammo for obvious reasons. I've run out of ammo fighting enemies to the point of frustration. Worst part is that heavy weapons are severaly restricted in their ammo use and being honest don't even feel worth using. Too slow, big, and clunky to be worth using especailly with their limited ammo supply which is actually the only reason why I've even bothered using them because I ran out of ammo lol. Again, if something ain't broke, don't fix it. (Edit: It gets better towards the end of the game after several upgrades. At first you will be struggling and you're going to have to get through that to get to the "goods.")
Storyline is boring as hell compared to ME1. At least it is to me anyway. I was interested in how the squad developed in ME1 and you could see the characters change when you did things for them or against them. Here? It's pretty much either they want to talk to you or they don't and it's pretty bland overall. At least Joker talks more tho I guess. (Edit: It's pretty much strictly based off completing missions for them now.)
The game has been over simplified. I kinda liked being able to choose from whatever I wanted and having a more complex game that just requires a little understanding than to have every single upgrade just be an attack boost and you don't really know by how much. Not to mention that the upgrade tree sucks. Sure you get more raw power out of it but you lose out on some of those awesome stats like improving your accuracy to the point where you could snipe with shotguns which worked and I enjoyed. Again, if something ain't broke don't fix it.
The interfaces are pretty bland. It's pretty much looking at boxes now. And then those boxes don't even give enough details just a bunch of mumbo jumbo. The only reason why they work is because of how over simplified the game is. Add anything else and the interface would be horrendous. Oh and good luck with that map now because you pretty much don't have one. You don't even have a radar anymore either. You wanna see where you're going? Gotta open up the map everytime and hope you don't take a wrong turn.
Nothing is explained well in the game which is kinda sad since things weren't explained well in ME1 but you could get a grasp of things without needing to go to guides. In ME2 I find myself constantly going to guides because of this. Some missions didn't give enough clues. One simple clue could have made the mission easier just by giving a general area to search instead of making you run around like mad.
The new space flight is stupid. Plain and simple. Not going to go into depth here because it's completely an opinion and instead of making it as simplified they made it more complex and time consuming.
Graphics are decent. Sound is good. Gameplay is meh, it's a shooter so what do you expect? Find things kill things. It's unique but has a gears of war feel to it with a twist. Dialogue is meh, I'm both a good and a bad guy but half the time I could only choose to act like a bad guy and I wasn't even given the choice where ME1 would almost always give you a choice.
You now have to pay attention to enemies HP bars as well because different weapons are ineffective against certain bars which really sucks. No more using your favorite weapon to blast through a level because on top of having ammo problems at one point and time or another it's gonna be useless and get you killed. Not to mention that the health bar and shield bar are now on top of one another as if in combined together and we all know how much combined HP bars suck.
The stores? What stores? There aren't any stores. You just upgrade your basic stuff and buy random crap there that doesn't even matter half the time. There's no more buying awesome things that you would get from your average everyday RPG game and there's no collecting the "best" items either. It's pretty much given to you and you use it and there aren't that many weapons in the game to begin with which leads back to my other point of the game being oversimplified and leaving the player feel unsatisfied. The game might as well be completely linear with the direction it has taken which is sad.
Overall a lot of changes weren't good and were made for no reason. At best I give this game a 6 out of 10. I have no idea why people say this was the best of the ME's. I haven't played 3 yet and with the way ME 2 is I don't even want to spend money on the next one. To me ME1 is the best hands down. The game has been simplified too much and the interface just feels wrong. Along witht he fact that certain changes were completely unnecessary (again if something ain't broke don't fix it). I only had a few gripes and complaints about ME1 and they were general things like more custimization and being able to carry more than 150 items etc. Just little leisures no game play changes or real changes to the game to actually make it more interesting and playable. This game is pretty much a failure to me. Some games rub off on people well, this one rubbed off on me the wrong way. If you haven't played ME1 go buy that game instead of this one. Otherwise just buy the game for the storyline because that's all you're going to get out of it. Not all changes are bad each weapon actually having a different function is nice for example but other changes will make you cringe like some team members only have 2 available weapons to use and weapons using ammo over heat.
I doubt you'll dislike the game as much as I did but I'm a pretty unbiased gamer and this is just how I feel about the game. Buy it and it won't feel like you've wasted that much money. The game isn't unplayable by any means and it's not that bad either. It's just that it has strayed too far from the original concept. If this were the first game of the series it wouldn't be that bad to me but because it's the second and so many unecessary changes were made it makes me dislike the game. It's a pretty straight forward game to the point that even a 5 year old could most likely play it now which can be both good and bad. Simple and easy to understand while at the same time so simple that things are left unexplaiend forcing the player to either go online to figure things out or do a lot of trial and errors which can get tideous at times. Just keep in mind that like all reviews this is strictly opinion based and whether or not you think this game is worth your time is up to you, not me. Just do a little research before buying it and see if you feel like it's worth playing. I found it 50/50. If it's on sale I'd say buy it and give it a go otherwise you're not missing out on much.
Oh the game is also filled with object collision bugs. I've pretty much been getting stuck on top of things with no way off except for loading up a save point. Quick save often or you might find yourself in a bit of discomfort.

“Digital happiness has done right job what horror game should really be in recent years.”
I’m pretty sure Dreadout is compared to Project Zero/Fatal Frame, but Dreadout shines in its own style. The story begins with a group of student trying to investigate an abandoned village. What I really like about Dreadout is how the atmosphere changes from daydream to nightmare.
Dreadout presents thick and haunting atmospheres. It feels dark, mysterious, and creepy everytime you take step into each area with great ambient soundtracks. The whole story encourages player to think and find reference from dialogues and notes. There is not much connection between Linda and side characters which make storyline feels pretty decent.
The solid part of Dreadout is gameplay as Linda can use her sense ability to discover item, puzzle, and incoming ghost. The way of game design and how you adapt your camera function to apply in each puzzle and ghost fight are genius and well executed. Most ghosts are both scary and fun to fight due to well-written script and how they behave to player in each encounter.
The graphics and animation are decent and some textures are too blurry for presentation. Moreover, the game has some gameplay glitch and poor optimization for some users like dropped framerate in school area. But I’m sure it can be easily fixed in future patch.
Dreadout surprises me in a lot of horror and gameplay aspects. It has variety and strong setup even the content is quite short. And the end holds me more questions, but for me it gives such a memorable experience which I hardly taste from other horror games in past few years.

Awesome point&click supernatural detective game. The game is broken down into several short case files where you find yourself investigating a crime and/or strange occurrence and then solving it. So far the case files have been fairly independent plots, only related by the same overall theme and detective duo. I like the "short story" style of this game since it fits my attention better. If you enjoyed playing point&click games like Blackwell and Kathy Rain then you'll definitely want this one.
The graphics/artwork are awesome - considering it's fairly blocky pixel art, it does an excellent job at conveying a lot of detail with its own unique style. The sound and music are also excellent with everything feeling very cohesive. The dialog is well written and amusing with likable characters that draw you into the story. I'm always surprised at how many point&click games seem to have trouble perfecting the simple, time-tested controls for this type of game - and thankfully in this case, these developers are some of the few who knew what they were doing. In terms of the user interface, everything just worked exactly as I hoped/expected it should work.
I hope this team puts out some more games in the future (or even some DLCs with more cases would be awesome since I'm sure i'll want more).

Glass Wing is a Banjo-style puzzle platformer with fantastic, N64-style ambience! It has varied areas and biomes just within the first 30 minutes of gameplay and it feels like new areas just keep coming, each one with stealth elements, tricky puzzles and that little pinch of something new every time.  It's polished like granite, and if Zelda was a horror series, Glass Wing would be part of it.
One of my favourite gameplay mechanics is the automatic jumping whenever you move over an edge - it means you can just lean back and concentrate on planning your moves instead of executing everything with pixel precision, making the gameplay more tactical and rewarding. Another cool thing is how items you can interact with stands out from the environment, making it really clear what you're supposed to do. In particular, the recovery hearts look really nice. And the way the title screen and file select menu is directly integrated in the game is really cool as well, giving you nothing that breaks immersion. The game also connects nicely to other works of the same dev and forms a coherent plot with callbacks and references to his previous games - if you know where to look.
On the flip side, though, it has several visual and aural glitches such as the Ferace dialogue looping if you cause the game to lag (might as well blame my WinXP PC for that, though :P) or Mayfly autojumping when going through certain doors which looks weird, but overall this doesn't taint my overall impressions of the game and I'm really recommending it!

Dreadout is a game done in a "Forgotten" Style of the Survival horror genre, and before you all say, "Um Cl0ps, there are alot of games done in First Person View with minimal lighting and so forth." Let me explain, so in a society where the Survival Horror Franchise is booming without a hitch, it's full of games, literally hundreds to thousands (Not including all the ♥♥♥♥ing zombie games.......thats a topic for another day) anyways, Dreadout attempts and accomplishes the forgotten art of Mortality. Now what I mean is we all played games like Evil Within, or Alien Isolation, Slender, Five nights at Freddy's, Outlast, etc. But in those games you don't really feel a sense of mortality, everything is sort of pushed along and given to you, sure you die and attempt again but thats not what I mean, most of the new games it's all given to you, Alien Isolation you learn very early on about the hiding aspects, Outlast you learn right away what effects lighting has and conserving batteries, so theres that and then theres that "Forgotten style" I spoke of, let's go back in time to December 13th 2001, A game is released in Japan, and is still held as one of the most scariest series of games of all time, Fatal Frame. Fatal Frame puts you into your character and basically says "Here is your ♥♥♥♥ing camera, heres how to work it, some♥♥♥♥♥♥is happening but you already knew that, escape, on your own because Im out the ♥♥♥♥ing door already because they don't pay me enough to deal with this♥♥♥♥♥♥" (lol) so you play through with subtle clues and hints of whats going on in books/tomes that you find or some of the ghosts you come across, but in the end it's up to you to figure♥♥♥♥♥♥out and take course of action. You feel mortality because your a normal human being dealing with this scary F'ed up situation where sometimes if you do die it is game over, you tend to be more cautious and♥♥♥♥♥♥seems more creepy and scary, and builds up until one crazy scare lets you release that sweet serenity of a scream/yelp/cry for help. Now Dreadout is like a modern day call to Fatal Frame, sort of like if Fatal Frame decided to have a F'ed up affair with resident evil, had a baby and said "do what you want but you only get to use a camera." and then silent hill came by to form a threesome and gave the baby some new toys to play with. (Seriously it;s a game worth playing until the heads of Fatal Frame in Japan get their heads out of their asses and finally release another of their masterpieces here in North America, that would raise the bar for a new generation.)
All in All let's face facts, it's not Fatal Frame........But, its not Duke Nukem Forever.

===Gameplay===
First of all, it's not the most original interface. We can see that it used elements from the Arkham series with the "detective vision". Controls were pretty clunky and confusing as well. It's nice for games in 3rd person to have similar controls so if we decide to drop the game for months on end, and then come back just to spend 5 minutes looking at the controls menu. With that being said, it's a good thing that the game only have 2 types of mobs since the controls aren't that well. Then there are extra things that you can explore and collect. Coming back with the controls, it's really difficult to collect items whenever you're near them. At the end of the game, the extra items are lazily tossed around the place and are pretty easy to find. You literally have to move around and angle your camera at a specific spot just for it to connect. Since this is also a detective game, the deductions don't reallly punish you when you get things wrong. There were 3 enforce symbols and if you use them all up, they drag you out of the deduction screen where you can just go back and guess every single clues that you found. Can't beat L.A. Noire I guess.  Finally, moving on to graphics. The in-game graphics are actually nice, but the cutscenes are♥♥♥♥♥♥ How do you mess that up?
===Content===
All I can say about Ronan is that he's pretty badass, but his backstory is so milked-out. Bad boy becomes cop, cop finds love, lover dies. His character model is really ♥♥♥♥ing nice, and I personally love the tats. A cop with an anarchist attitude. Unfortunately, the only characters you only need to know are Ronan and Joy (his annoying complaining teen psychic sidekick). The story line is actually creative and very interesting. I had my assumptions at first, but I was a part right. Apparently the Bell Killer was actually Abigail Williams, a young girl whom accused many innocent people for witchcraft who was then shortly executed. The judge found out and lynched her for doing so; however, before her death-- she drew a bell symbol and vowed that she'd finish her task of exterminating witches. For centuries she has been a lost soul possessing body after body to kill young girls who are mediums (which she beleived are witches) the many witch-lynching methods and disposes the killers' bodies by killing them. That's why Ronan died. He unknowingly killed a girl but was possesed by Abagail, which was a pretty good twist in my opinion. The flow of the story was well-paced. I didn't appreciate how some maps were recycled, but the story honestly drove the game. After all, mystery stories always has the best twists.

This is a lovely little gem of a game that is just oozing with warmth and "feel good"-ness. While by no means a cakewalk, the action is generally quite mellow and relaxed, perfect for unwinding after a stressful day, or just spending a lazy weekend lounging around with it. Objectively speaking, I'd give the game an 8/10, increase that to a 9/10 if you've played and liked a game from the Atalier series or something similar, or if you are the sort that finds adorable little anime girls irresistable.

Okay, so I clicked that I recommend the game because there's not 'recommend with caveats' button.
Let's get the obvious things out of the way: Owlboy is gorgeous. The art is top-notch, the music is fantastic, the attention to detail in the smallest custom sprite animations, etc, is stunning. Moving around the rather unique game world feels fluid and natural. And over all, Owlboy is an okay game.
Yeah, just okay. And just kind of... a game. It's vaguely a twin stick shooter. It's a bit of a metroidvania, a bit of a puzzler, sometimes a set-piece stealth game. It doesn't really have an identity. It doesn't have unified gameplay, and it suffers for it. It feels more like a sequence of things to do than it does a game. A few of the boss fights are solid, but over all, the gameplay is bland and the sequences wear out their welcome all too fast. It's an 8 hour game that could have been 4 hours long without losing anything.
The characters are not especially evocative. A few side characters here and there are charming, and most of the characters have a shining moment or two, but they never come off as particular distinct or likeable, nor do they have fleshed out character arcs. The story has its ups - a very stunning moment or two - but like everything with Owlboy, it's too thin. It's mixed in with hours of little-to-no story but also little-to-no gameplay.
The game has wacky difficulty balancing. Sometimes, it feels like a kid's game, almost insultingly easy, then a sequence will slam you with incredibly precise timing and instant death punishments. Sometimes, in the game's lack of identity, it becomes very, very unclear what exactly the game wants from you. And while the movement and jumping and flying are very smooth, you spend a lot of the game cycling between companions that you have to carry about to use their abilities, and switching between them/lifting and dropping them is a bit of a headache. It functions fine for the Lost Viking style puzzles, but when suddenly you have to switch between them and activate their abilities back and forth during a hectic boss fight, it gets unacceptably muddy, especially for a game of this production quality.
So, do I recommend Owlboy? Well, I don't NOT recommend Owlboy, but it's not an art piece game that will leave you thinking, and it's not a story game that will leave you interested, and it's not an action game that will leave you adrenalized. It's just sort of a pretty thing to look at and experience and then go about your day, mostly unaffected.
It isn't a bad game, but it's just sort of a game.

In case it isn't obvious from the number of hours I've played, I really like this game. A big part of this is the politics side of nation building. For example, you can't just declare war without a reason and people won't like it when you do. War is there but not in the depth of something like the Total War series. There is also a lot of court intrigue that it pays to keep an eye on or your continent spanning empire will crumble into civil war and other nations will snap up your provinces. Paradox do s a great job supporting the game with heaps of free content, even if you don't buy the DLC. Also, do yourself a favour and avoid save-scumming. You will lose wars and suffer the humiliation of begging for mercy but that just makes your inevitable return and the crushing of your foes more satisfying.

Before anyone is going to rage at me here for this... I LOVE this game... and i wanted so so so so hard to give it a "YES"... But i just have many reasons why i didnt. I try to do this relatively Spoiler free!
This is gooing to be a bit lengthy... so bare with me... i will put a tl:dr at the very bottom of this.
The Background Idea for Owlboy was as it seems aspired by Kid Icarus, Super Mario 3 and has to me at least certain Zeldaesque Elements. The Game was in Development since 2007. Certain points clearly show this... others sadly dont.
The Game was created by D-Pad Studio. I sadly never played anything they made before.
The Story is a very basic "Save the World scenario", not to spoiler too much, There are Very Powerful Relics wich came from a very old Owl Civilisation, they stand in the Focus of Resoring the World, or Destroying it again.
We play as a small semi-anthromorphic Little boy named Otus. He seems to be born as a Mute, wich explains why he does not talk. He is shown as a weakling with no real Skills or anything. A Pure dissapointment  for his Mentor. He can walk, Fly, and Dash. Also his main Purpose is to carry around other characters, wich will aid him with firepower, or other gadgets, to make his way through the game possible.
Sadly Otus is one of the most... interchangeable characters i have EVER seen in my life. He is a Mute, wich makes him unable to speak, this is perfectly fine and used very well as a story element. Yet Otus never seems to grow during the whole Story... nothing that happens really lets him shine in what he does. He is always scared and always weak. He never stands up for his friends and feels in a lot of cases just like the Taxi for his Party. "Hey Otus, pick me up so i can shoot this enemy there... please thank you! In Zeldaesque games, we at least have the Feel of the Main character growing with the Story. Getting Stronger, getting smarter about what is happening. Otus is just kept very small for the entirety of the Game, Everyone else knows ore, can do more, and is more important for the overall story.
The Gameplay is to put is simple... decent. I really liked it, the Controls were a bit wonky at times, switching out your Teammates to solve puzzles on the fly is quite fun. I think the game for what it is... Is a bit too Simple at times... and at other times insanely frustrating because certain enemys just annoy you to fight against (the Beebirds in the Darkness level) because of numbers. Mini Bossfights always follow the same Pattern: 1 Enemy, 2 Enemys, 3 Enemys... and so on up to 8 enemys. That was no fun and got frustrating very soon.
Another big letdown for me were the "final" bosses of each "dungeon" Memorize the very very simple patterns and you are Good to go. It is from WTF to "oh when i stay here, the enemy wont be able to hit me anymore... yay".
Here we come to the point where this game truly truly shines... the graphics are some of the most beautifully, lovely crafted Pixelarts you have and will ever see. Every detail is nice and crisp. Truly.. Lovely!
I played this on my Keyboard and the Controls felt very smooth. They do what they must, and they never really feel... "sloppy" or bad.
The Game Clocks in at about 10 Hours. Very Few Dungeons, no real collectibles, nothing to really power up your character. The Dungeons are on a very easy to normal level of difficulty, and mostly you find the right solution to a Puzzle in a matter of seconds, because the Game shows you anything, and barely encourages you to think for yourself. Making it more of a rush.
Owlboy is such a great and lovely game, with so many loveable characters. I would just squeak and hug Solus (another cutie owl) all day and take care of him. Sadly his "plot" twist does absolutely not work with his overall character... but hey... plot twist... guess they can do anything they want in the end.

Would you read or watch a trilogy and then stop right before the end? Do you like cliffhangers that will never be resolved? Do you like to having the feeling you are in control while playing a game, only to be railroaded into doing something stupid later on? No? Then this game is not for you. Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2 are solid, if not excellent games. They have their flaws, but I can live with them. But it is a continuous storyline that runs across three games, not two. Mass Effect 3, the third installment, not available on Steam, but only on Origin, has a very controversial ending that ends the trilogy on a sour note. If you've somehow missed the controversy, just google Mass Effect 3 ending, read some of the many things that have already been said about it, and weep. Weep for the loss of something that could have been epic. Weep for the hurt feelings of countless gamers. Weep for the sorry fate of a couple of epic fictional characters, that felt like friends to so many of us.
If you think you will be able to live with the above and also love RPGs, and especially if you liked Mass Effect, then by all means, buy this game now, no hesitation, just make sure to get the Digital Deluxe Edition and the various add ons. Or just keep reading and then make up your mind.
Mass Effect 2 continues the story that began in Mass Effect, but with some changes. You need to assemble a new crew and won't be able to play with your friends from Mass Effect, with two exceptions, although there is DLC that will allow you to play, briefly, alongside Liara as well. A very large part of the game is spent assembling a team for a mission that will determine the fate of the Galaxy. Although it is a roundabout way, it does allow you to make new friends and new enemies alike. With a better game engine, the game looks far better than Mass Effect and is much less dated. You can now select additional actions, good or bad, to determine how your character, Shepard, is viewed. The various classes are structured differently from the first game and you no longer get a new weapon every 10 metres, there are far fewer flavours availble. But although it is certainly different from Mass Effect, it is not vastly different. The voice acting is excellent, the music is good, the storyline could be a bit better and straightforward, but is still very good. In and of itself, it is arguably the best game in the series.
The only real drawback of this game is the lack of a satisfying ending in Mass Effect 3. So be aware of that before you purchase this game.

The game itself feels like a stripped down Fatal Frame with a whole bunch of Indonesian ghost lore.
If you wanna skip the lengthy part of my review and go straight to the pros and cons, you can find them below.
But first things first: the story.
You play as the Indonesian high school student Linda and you're just coming back from a trip with your school class. Your teacher drives down a road until she notices a blocked off bridge leading to an abandoned village. You don't know how you came here but you all decide to investigate. After investigating the village you find yourself in the school located there. Something terrible happens and you're trapped. Alone. Your main objective: get the hell out of this place!
Linda herself has special abilities which make her sense and see supernatural beings that are nearby as well as items of interest.
To stay with the story, it isn't too bad actually. The game is comprised of three acts, act 0, act 1 and act 2. Act 0 acts as a foreshadowing to act 1 and act 2 is the continuation of act 1, released almost over a year after the initial game release.  The story centers around a big chunk of supernatural beings from Indonesian folklore and has many twists to it. Also there are two endings to be achieved. Personally, I got one of the endings and it wasn't bad at all. Also, after act 1 the game gets much less cliché, effectively making everything more enjoyable.
But... what about the gameplay? Well, here are the basics:
You can run, walk, interact with a lot of doors and items and use your IrisPhone (harhar) to take photos. The camera is the key mechanic of the game. Taking photos is used to defeat ghosts and solve puzzles, the camera vision is also used to uncover hidden passages, invisible ghosts and progress through the game.
Then there's the dying mechanic. And by that I mean: you can not "die". You may fail, but you will never get a "game over" screen. Once a ghost defeats you, you will end up at Limbo. From there you may head to a bright light and you'll be given a chance to go at it again.
Also you may collect some items along the way. Even though there is an inventory, there is no combining of items to solve puzzles in any way. Which is kind of a shame, the game had some potential there.
Since this is a horror game, the horror oughtta be there, right?
Well, it is. As soon as it is nighttime, ghosts start to show up. When encountering some of them for the first time, they can be pretty scary. Through act 0 you will only encounter two of the many ghosts in the game - one of which is a heavy one. You can only sense it and see it through your camera, so when you need to get someplace fast but know there is a ghost breathing down your neck, you're kinda on edge. Act 1 features much more ghosts and if you're not prepared or know how to fight them or successfully get away from them you will get scared a lot. But after a while in act 1, you will know how to deal with those entities and then defeating them kinda loses its scaryness. So the horror doesn't last long. Until act 2, that is.
For act 2 brings out a much wider variety of ghost mechanics that will put you on edge if you're playing it for the first time because you will get into situations where you just don't know what to do about them.
But the horror doesn't only lie in the ghosts themselves. Act 2 does a lot with its surroundings. I won't spoiler anything though, but let me tell you this much: mirrors are the worst. Aside from that the game does underline its horror a lot with sounds and music, sudden turns of events and a couple of very well-placed jumpscares.
It is quite rare that I appreciate jumpscares but the jumpscares in this game are just perfect. You'll never expect them, they will always catch you off guard and they aren't just cheap screamers with overly loud sound. They're good.
So overall, the horror in this game will wear off quite quickly during act 1, but that only leads you into a false sense of security because act 2 is just so much different.
But speaking of music, the soundtrack of this game features some really nice themes that are doing their job well. Some of them aren't for the horror of the game. These tracks just sound good.
Back to the ghosts: A nice thing about this game is that every supernatural being you will encounter actually is a thing from Indonesian lore people in the real world believe in. That's a nice little detail. I adore that.
Of course, not everything is good about the game. But this isn't about plot holes, boring combat or anything.
The main issue I am going to adress here are the horrendous loading times and the performance which sometimes goes BAD. Also the texture resolution is still hilariously awful and doesn't justify the loading times one tiny bit. Seriously, I thought I forgot some options in the options menu but nope, the textures are just blurry and I can't do anything about it.
On occassion this game's performance sucks♥♥♥♥♥ I mean, you're running around, moving your camera and BAM! you look in the opposite direction because the game was frozen for half a second and turned you around. Really annoying at night when you can't see sh*t. And the loading times are just awful. I don't even understand why they are so god damn awful. It's nothing on my end, that's for sure.
On the technical side of things, I didn't get any crashes whatsoever. Just some bugs sometimes.
On occasion the world won't load fully so you'll se the surroundings pop in one by one. And then there's starting from act 1 or act 2 which sometimes causes game breaking glitches. A restart usually fixes this however.
Well, what else about the game?
It has got some little details to it that I want to point out here before switching to the pros and cons.
If you beat the game once you will be able to go to the back of the car in act 1 and choose between a selection of different outfits for Linda once you start a new game. Some traditional outfits as well as some casual outfits.
This game has some pretty nice effects, especially when interacting with some of the ghosts (one in particular that shows up in act 2) up close.
And the game has boob physics. Yay...?
Also, there's a ton of eastereggs to find. Some are related to the developers, some are related to other horror games and some are just silly little things to brighten up your day.
Oh and the English translation is sometimes... hilarious. Yeah. Hilarious. Let's leave it at that.
So, off to the pros and cons.
Pros:
+ A semi-open world for you to explore, find hidden items, secrets and eastereggs
+ A variety of different settings, you didn't honestly think all the spookyscariness will be in that school, did you?
+ The supernatural beings are all reminiscent of Indonesian folklore
+ Solid horror that will keep you on edge upon getting to act 2 because it changes up things dramatically
+ Very good sounds and music
+ Story's not all bad and got a lot of unexpected turns, some stuff can be foreseen though
+ Good English voiceover, good animation quality, nice character design
+ Impressive jumpscares
+ Big ghost variety
+ Runs well most of the time, no crashes
+ Boob physics
+ Female protagonist (that's always a plus)
Cons:
- You cannot die
- The texture quality on the environment tends to be sub standard
- Sometimes your framerate drops to 0 for half a second, effectively annoying the hell out of you
- The horror in act 1 wears off quickly
- Once you know how to deal with most enemies, killing them gets quite trivial (act 2 fixes a lot of this though)
- Some achievements fail to work a lot of times
- There's only two acts, wish there were more
-+ Dat English translation tho
Would I recommend this game? Yes.
The horror's pretty decent and at the current price I'd call it commendable.
Also it's nice to play an Indonesian horror game for a change.

Let me start with saying that this game is moderately good, but it has some insanely annoying bugs and way too high price for an indie game (asking $10 for this is actually hilarious).
Now, let's get into specifics.
First and foremost, controls are bugged. You can't move+accelerate, until the level hasn't loaded yet (you'll just end up stuck at the start, if you'll hold the buttons). Also, the controls aren't really responsive -- there's this "lag", when you press the buttons, but don't move just yet, for a few milliseconds. This might not seem big, but since this whole game is about right timing, this is actually crucial (especially if you're trying to set a record).
Second of all, achievements are bugged to a point of no return. I'm an achiever -- I love to farm achievements, and I was pretty disappointed when even the easiest achievement weren't unlocking, even after 3-4 repeats. This annoys me a lot (possibly more than it should).
Third of all, game is extremely repetitve. You can move, you can burst, you see traps, and... that's it. There'll be a few variations of traps, granted. But the core gameplay won't change at all.
Lastly, dev isn't friendly at all -- I've seen people banned in the official discussions for calling dev rude (not even using any curse words whatsoever).
And, of course, as I've already mentioned, the price is inadequate for this product. For $10 you can buy a much better polished game with a lot less repetitive gameplay (especially during some sale).
Would I recommend buying this game? No, I would not. If this game would've costed around $1, maybe it'd be worth checking out (with all the bugs fixed, that is). So, if you enjoy platformers/runners/time attack games -- play some
, or something similar.

I'll be honest, this game isn't that bad. The game plays very well and I enjoyed it a lot! And to say this game was made in Gamer Maker impresses me! However, this game isn't without it's faults.
The enemies in this game are completely optional to kill. You just need to run past them. I attempted to kill one of them... I finally succeeded, but I wasted about 10 minutes of my time as they didn't reward me in anyway. The worlds feel completely empty with nothing to collect and the puzzles get rehashed over, and over. This game is comparable to Banjo-Kazooie..... that is if you take out the fun characters, objectives, open world, and collectibles. This game also loves, loves, loves, LOVES it's Super Mario Sunshine platforming stages as it throws the stages against you multiple times throughout the game.
This title had it's moments. But the longest stages for me in this game were the times when there were VERY precise jumps that I would have to try again and again and again to make. This combined with rehashing level designs is artificially making this game feel longer.
Oh, and be warned... this game has an auto jump that is comparable to Zelda. But to be honest... I didn't mind this feature too much as I had to do some back tracking as I missed one of the few collectibles in the game as I glitched through one of the early stages thanks to the auto jump. And due to this game rehashing some of the same level designs for a while, I was able to pull this glitch off and skip many tedious parts of the game.
For some reason, despite all of this, I somehow enjoyed the game. Would I recommend this game? Absolutely!....... at a cheaper price. This game is not worth $5. I would only recommend this title in a bundle or if this game goes under $1 in a sale. Just be warned.... there is a glitch at the end of the game that refuses to let you past a endless revolving door after a certain rehash of a certain stage.

So I start up the game and configure my controls, only to find that left and right are swapped, for some reason. I start my review with this because it is the first of many things that show what a mess this game turns out to be.
Though let me get the positives out of the way. Firstly, it looks ok. While this would normally not be a compliment, I am used to these kinds of graphics from a mediocre Unity game, not something made in Game Maker (I only figured this out when I got to the ice section). Also your character has a metroid ball with working bomb jumps. Finally, the music is kinda cool.
However, despite those positives, it seems like the developers, despite knowing how to code, have zero experience with game design. Firstly, the difficulty goes all over the place, with it's apex in a desert level in the middle of the game, and it's nadir right before the end. Second, while the graphics look kinda nice, there is no artistic cohesion, one minute you are in a forest, and the next a factory jumping from logs to metal boxes and it feels very disjointed. Thirdly there are several Gamemaker 3D specific problems. You can't customize the graphics, the character's shadow stays the same size, but magically disappears after a certain point, the camera loves clipping through walls, the camera starts out incredibly zoomed in, ice doesn't reflect properly (that's how I figured out it was Gamemaker), and you clip through the world in the final level (the untextured skybox is an ugly color).
These minor complains could all be forgiven, however, if the gameplay was any good. I can understand why people compare it to an N64 game, there are only 4 buttons for everything. The problem with this is that approximately 100 percent of your useful actions are bound to jump or spindash, causing you to become a ball when you meant to spin. using your items is awkward because the character has the reach of a 4 year old and it's not clear if you need to get closer to hit thorns or if they will hurt you. Your character moves at the speed of butter in a freezer and flying is the most awkward experience ever, due to your ability to easily fly backwards and upside down. Worst of all, though, if you manage to die, you go back to the needless interactive menu and, once you load, to a checkpoint that could be up to 10 minutes away, even in a best case scenerio, the time to recover is at least 20 seconds, when it could be 1-3.
The puzzles are a myrad better in that they are merely bad. Some are ok, but others are just "use item at a location" and the actual puzzle is just finding where to go. Honestly, though, they aren't worth getting the game for, not by any stretch of the imagination. It is like buying Metroid for the puzzle of "shoot red door with missile."
It's clear that the developers worked very hard on this game, but it's also clear they don't understand how to make games fun; if you worked on this game and are reading this please take note. Before you release anything, please get people who are outside your circle (or at least not friends) to playtest it, I know it hurts like seeing your kid torn to shreds but it will give you good feedback. Oh, and please get Unity, at least the personal edition, at least to improve as game developers. And good luck on future projects. As for consumers considering buying this, consume elsewhere.
Edit: sorry if I come off as cynical in this review, in truth I just feel like this game could have been so much more, and that's why I bothered to put three hours into writing some (hopefully) constructive criticism.

I'm 72 years old and these have been the best 20 hours of my life.
EDIT::
After playing through the game multiple times, including finishing it on Honour Mode, I have to say that my opinion of this game is even higher than it was after those first 20 hours. After finishing this game, it feels like my life is complete and there's nothing left to live for. This may be the last game I ever play and review I ever write. I would like to thank Larian for filling a void that has been plaguing me for more than half a century.
I found the main story as well as every single side quest/story to be fun and interesting. There are no boring fetch quests as far as I can tell. How you handle side quests and whether you complete them or not 'does' affect the ending; as such, they could be considered extensions of the main story. (You could be unsatisfied with the ending if you just rush through and skip things.)
You can build your characters any way you see fit and almost any build is completely viable. If you don't like the way you built your characters, just wait until you complete Act 1 and you can rebuild them any way you want as frequently as you want all the way up to the very end of the game; this is very good for testing new things out. By the end of the game my main character was a fire breathing Geo/Pyro battle mage that wielded a fire staff, used Warfare skills and showered my enemies in meteors with some necromancy for physical damage in case the enemy had too much resistance to those elements; she was pretty godly. I plan on trying a solo Honour mode run next with a similar but more diverse build. (I love the lizards!)
For me, the best part of this game is the combat. It's extremely well done and very fun.
I can't really say any more than what the other reviews cover though. Just know that if a fight seems absolutely impossible, that it really isn't. I've gone into fights where half my party was annihilated before I got to do anything, yet I still emerged victorious. There's always a way to win even if the enemy has you outnumbered and outleveled; just gotta think!
Like many reviews state, there are still some bugs. As far as I can tell, they are all minor. After multiple play throughs on multiple difficulties I have not experienced any major bugs. Nothing game breaking and nothing that really affected my gameplay much.
The few bugs I've experienced:
- Many unvoiced lines in Arx.
- Incorrect journal entries.
- Sometimes a character would act blind in combat even though they weren't (could't use any ranged skills, couldn't see around themselves, but this was rare and only lasted a single turn.)
- Sometimes the enemy AI would derp out and they'd just run around or repeatedly climb up and down a ladder until they were out of AP.
- Custom undead characters do not receive the appropriate immunities, such as bleeding and suffocation. (though I don't recall any of my characters ever being afflicted with Bleed...) (Fane does receive these immunities)
- Undead afflicted with Decay will not attempt to avoid poison puddles (Not sure if this is a bug or an oversight).
- Altitude does not affect many player or enemy melee attacks. (Entities 10+ meters above can be struck with melee.) But it does affect some skills, such as Dragon's Blaze, Laser Ray, charging skills, Battle Stomp, etc.
... I think that's about it. I'll add more if I remember them.
Some reviews complain about enemies being omniscient and knowing all of your strengths and weaknesses (including whether you're undead or not), which is true, but it's also true for players. Any player with Loremaster on one of their characters can examine any NPC or enemy to gain insight into their strengths and weaknesses. Only one of your characters needs Loremaster. If you examine with someone that doesn't have it, they use the skill level of whoever does, even if that person is dead. (This even works on the final boss, at no point in the game is it unfair that enemies can spot your weaknesses.)
So in summary, very fun game, great character customization, great combat, good story, a few minor bugs. It can be challenging in some scenarios but it's supposed to be; that's at least half the fun. I could mention the poor inventory management but countless reviews already cover that.
Tip: Carry a couple pieces of +Thievery and +Loremaster gear with you to make sure you can pick any lock and identify any item. There may be times when your base skill isn't sufficient.
TL;DR: Recommended, as shown above.

Frequent pauses in the form of looking for power ups keeps the action from getting too monotonous, leaving you with nice pacing and a little breather in between hard fights. And there are plenty of those on the higher difficulties. But don't expect to come away from these little pauses without a few surprises, the developers definitely like to keep you on your toes.
The game is quite short, though the free DLC almost doubles the number of missions and a survival mode gives it some extra replayability.
The way the in game menus are handled is a great touch, you're never taken out of the environment to click through a pop up window and there is no dedicated "use" button. Simply walk up to a terminal and your mouse cursor automatically appears to let you interact with it, very nice!
One tip, don't bother upgrading the two starting weapons until later in the game. Some of the unlocks (especially the grenade launcher) are much more useful (and fun).
