The 'Metro' games are excellent. Though they’re based off the popular post apocalyptic fiction book by Dmitri Glukhovsky, Metro Last Light does not follow the story line in the book, instead it is a direct sequel to Metro 2033 (the game and book). Last Light is a game I believe everyone should try.
The attention to detail is phenomenal, every part of the Metro has been carefully engineered with precision to create the look of a worn and dying civilization. This attention to detail creates an immersive and atmospheric game.
The game's plot is excellent. The Metro is very atmospheric and immersive thanks to the excellent graphics, the slow paced solo guitar music and the excellent plot. I won't go into detail as I don't want to ruin the story for anyone who hasn't had the pleasure of experiencing the Metro games. Essentially you, Artyom, wipe out the Dark Ones with a plethora of nuclear bombs - or so you thought. Intense radiation plagues the streets, which has caused mutation in many species turning them violent, untamable and monstrous. On the way you meet people, discover the civilizations (Hanza, Reich, The Order) and have a great time.
Overall this game is a must play from me, works great on PC with keyboard and mouse, and I'm guessing a controller would work well too. The game has great gunplay and a stellar story, which can be let down by the feeling that the game throws hordes of enemies at you for nothing else than to make you have more game time. The music and SFX are good but the voice acting feels lacking for some but most characters are excellently voice acted.

MURDERED has a cool concept and plot: You have been murdered and trying to solve your own murder as a ghost. What is not cool, however, is how repetitive and confusing this game can get.
The game is a glorified movie with a few cuts of brain-dead gameplay here or there. Your objective will tell you to go to a location. Then you will use to stealth to kill some demons, then you will pickup all the clues to solve a few "questions" which lead you to another location. Rinse and repeat a few times.
The crux of the game should be solving hard puzzles, but most puzzles are just wandering around a small room and mashing 'E' on everything to 'reveal' it. Then you have unlimited tries to put the 'clues' together (there is NO penalty for guessing wrong, not even a special perfect ending). Additionally, the demon fighting game play is ridiculously easy. I realized half-way through that you could actually run past every demon without fighting them. In other words, there is no challenge.
One final thing I didn't like: No mini-map in-game. It turns out you only could get a mini-map if you PREORDERED the game (for something so core you would think it would just come with the game). If you are a completionist this makes collecting everything a living hell. Every wall in the town looks the same. And some collectibles don't appear unless you go along all the walls and mash a button (in other words, this is near-impossible without a guide).

Dangerous High School Girls in Trouble!™ was a real surprise for me. The game lets you create a gang of high schoolers who decide to rebel against authority and uncover (very) dark secrets in a 1920's American town. You do that by playing mini-games, using different stats you can raise or temporarily boost during the game. They're entertaining and sometimes pretty funny, but the real interest is the main story which does an amazing job of conveying the oppressive atmosphere of a secretive town that will do anything to protect itself and subdue our young heroines. This IS a fairly dark story - these girls are definitely in Trouble!™
I was surprised to find myself so attached to the characters: they don't have amazingly developed personalities, but the artwork does a lot to help differentiate them. I just reached the end of my first game and I felt bad about getting a lackluster ending for my characters so I immediately started a new one, something I was not expecting when i started. The girls you can pick for your party are also a pretty diverse bunch, which is nice, although they could have expanded on that a bit (for example, one of them is implied to be gay by others and has no options to flirt with boys, but nothing comes of it, when one of the main themes of the game is the pressure put on young girls to marry early). Still, I appreciate the effort.
The presentation of the game is both charming and...a little confusing. The layout isn't very polished (but then again this game came out in 2008) with some annoying little flaws and the rules of some games are a bit convoluted. But I love the way it emulates an actual board game and incorporates this into the main story as much as possible.
Overall, the developers suggest playing this game in short bursts, and I agree with this advice, although there's a real chance to get sucked in by the story, like I did. I'd recommend it to anyone interested either by the atmosphere or the weird board game-rpg hybrid gameplay - it's pretty much unlike anything else I've played.

Nexuiz is a competent futuristic tournament combat game with demanding although attractive DirectX11 graphics.  As is often the case with tournament combat games, the backstory is paper thin and serves only to briefly explain the futuristic setting.  While the combat is quick paced, and there are a variety of fun mutators like super jumps or unlimited ammo, the game unfortunately looks and feels almost identical to Unreal Tournament 2004.  This may not be a bad thing for fans of the genre because the game will immediately feel familiar, but I found myself growing bored quickly and the lackluster weapon effects and HUD did not do much to encourage my enthusiasm.  That said, it is a competent entry in the genre but the lack of a single player campaign, steep system requirements, and rather lackluster gameplay should keep all but genre diehards away.

It's a weird fusion of adventure game/point-and-click game with a board game. I opened it up expecting to just try playing it for a few minutes and then spending the better part of a weekend on it. I remember the story being really fun and compelling me to keep playing. The minigames have an addictive quality too, at first; but as most of the negative reviews say, they start feeling repetitive eventually (which is why I'm pretty sure I never finished it.) It sucks because the story makes you want to find out what happens next asap, but the game suffers if you don't play it at a casual pace. I'm looking forwards to giving it another (slower) try.
(Also: it only takes up like 24 MB, so if you get bored of it and don't intend to play it for a few months, you won't feel like you're wasting harddrive space by not uninstalling it.)
Since it's such an oddball of a game and it's probably nigh-impossible for many people to guess whether they'll enjoy it or not, try getting it on sale. (I'd say it's worth 10 USD for sure and $15 maybe, but $20 is a little much.) For people who like checking out unusual gameplay or are intrigued by the story premise, it's definitely worth a shot. It's a very novel experience you that you might end up enjoying a lot.

To summarise - an atmospheric, rewarding and compelling game. There are other sources to explain how the game works so I won't re-explain that but I will highlight its key points.
You build a deck of equipment and encounters, then run the level with that deck of cards, making progress towards expanding your deck (and thus your options), and in the middle of all that you engage in short third-person fights with creatures/enemies. And in the middle of ALL of that, you are continually listening to the comments of the dealer, the writing for which is superb and the voice acting for which really sets a very mysterious and compelling tone to the game. Added to that the animation as all this takes place, the atmosphere of the game is extremely enticing, full of exploration, mystery and intrigue.
The deck building is compelling as it has a real impact on how you will play the level and has more depth that 'best equipment in, worst equipment out', actually requiring thought to get cards which may work well with your building of the encounters. Speaking of which, you also choose what the encounters are going to be during the level, mainly focusing on ones which you have not completed yet which in turn will expand your available cards. A very rewarding and compelling loop with surprising depth.
The little battles are not too long or onerous and as they are very short and there is a lot of variety (some variety in enemies and variety in how you play based on what equipment you've managed to acquire, completely changing your abilities) they do not get repetitive quickly.
The campaign is, as I have said, very atmospheric. It is all about exploring the encounters around you (as you don't know which ones they are), with success leading to rewards expanding your deck for the next run. There is a fair element of luck involved, which would be annoying if it weren't for the fact that you make permanent progress on each run even if you die, which means that you still feel like something was achieved.
Overall, these factors combine to make a very compelling and enjoyable experience which is highly recommended for just about everyone, since it isn't really just a 'brawler' or a 'card building game' or any of those, but a great hybrid which takes the best elements from everything in my opinion. Add to that the updates by the developers, it is one to pick up and keep playing. (And the DLC also comes highly recommended as it adds yet another element to this great game!)

An addicting wee game with some issues.
It's a very fun game with likeable characters, a fun idea and an interesting theme that seems weirdly addictive for how simple it is.
There are a few gripes that may bother you and make it less fun and you should be well aware of these.
The main gripe is that this game is very much a victim of the RNG a lot of the time. You might get 10 customers in your shop suddenly and think "This is great!" ... then you notice 5 of them are little girls who generally won't give you much profit whatsoever. You'll be nearing a payment dead line for your loan and suddenly your biggest selling product will become very common and will reduce in half for the price or you'll want to sell and instead you'll suddenly be pestered by dozens of people just wanting to sell you stuff instead or want to place orders for AFTER your loan date.
It's one of those games where if you get to day 30 and suddenly realise you only have like 50K, you pretty much aren't going to win the game. There is no real way to pull a rabbit out of the hat and you might as well just restart the game which is quite frustrating when you put 10 hours into the game and realise that you're pretty much screwed.
The dungeon fighting is fun but a bit repetitive after awhile, especially since there is honestly a very small selection of loot to pick from and you will soon get annoyed at how restrictive the game is based on the 'time units'.
You get 4 time units a day and lose these with certain tasks. Opening your store to sell is 1 unit, going to town to meet characters (which I enjoy but it seems a punishment since meeting a friend takes away a lot of your selling day which makes the game feel punishing if you try and enjoy their story) but going to the dungeons cost 2 time units. Sometimes you'll go to the dungeon and get nothing in drops and you're limited to only doing 5 dungeon floors at a time and these can be done in 5 minutes.
I would certainly advise you to look through the wiki when you buy the game since honestly they don't give you much information in the game for tutorials and I didn't even hear about things like 'exp-chaining' until I looked through the wiki. It makes the games a lot easier.
Pretty much if you're playing the game on the first play through I would just advise you to grind out as much money as possible and ignore trying to make friends with the characters since it seems pretty hard to do if you're unexperienced.
I would still recommend the game for a fun little time if you can look past these small annoyances.

in KW2:B you can choose between 3 distinct races to fight with: Humans, Orcs and Elves. They might be what you would expect from each race, but that's not really an issue as they made them really well!
Humans are pretty basic and medieviel-ish, except they can breed FREAKING DRAGONS! and can train mages, otherwise what you would expect (each race has their heroes, Dwarven "Mercenaries", Mages and Dragons.
Orcs - Quantity over Quality - they are really dumb but that makes them fun to play! it's a bit hard getting used to them, as they infinitely spawn at your base (can be toggled) but once you got into it it's relatively easy.
Elves - Quality over Quantity - these guys are a bit tricky, as you need to "build" trees in order to build Buildings on it, but they have some neat advantages like a wood gathering spirit.
Each race can unlock new buildings, Units, Abilities etc..... (permanently with materials - will cover later) and for each upgrade you make you can see your tribe grow in the main menu, which is a neat feature, although i haven't recognized much difference on single upgrades - but are clearly noticeable when doing more.
Once your done upgrading, you can buy Battle cards to aid you in your fights. Cards range from Resources, to units and even timed bonuses.
Materials for crafting these Upgrades or Cards can be gathered by completing matches (win or lose) beating every 3 waves in survival, trading or simply by logging in each day - which is IMO a great idea to keep people interested in the game.
KW2:B has a few game modes BUT keeps growing! currently has 5 game modes:
- Capture town flag: Get your Army through the Enemy gates and capture the Town center to beat them.
- Total Annihilation: Destroy and murder everything from that player to beat them.
- Capture the flag: there is a flag in the middle of the map, you know the drill!
-Casualties of War: just murder as many Enemies as possible to win - has a set limit to win
- Zombie Survival: like capture town flag, except you have to defend it agains masses of incoming Zombies! pretty hard especially with humans as you can't really get to stone and gold with them.
Battles start relatively fast in KW2:B and can be really exciting and pretty frustrating if you just wanna take things easy. But once you got everything set and rush into **** with your team it's a whole lot of fun! But Beware! Killed people can TURN!! so, if you just leave the corpses around they could suddenly stand up and start clawing at you! ways to deal with that fu***rs is by burning them (dead or living.....again) or by tasking your workers to scavenge the corpses.
It can especially be fun to let a few peasants die near the enemy camp just to see them turn! >:)
Haven't gone into this (cause i think i'm to bad for this :P) but it has PvP and PvE. You can also do a Zombie Survival run with a Friend!
I usually be veeeery careful on who to call a good dev, but those very few guys working on making the Game great are really amazing! the Game tend to have some issues and when this arises the devs jump on this and try their damn hardest fixing them. They are also really well present in the Forums and are up for new things and suggestions.
Overall a great RTS Game that WILL grow much better, I'm sure of it!

One of the few games these days that are just plain fun to play with other people.
First of all, it had local coop, but to my surprise I had discovered that you can play local coop as well as online coop simultaneously, that is, you and your friends can play together on one screen whilst going up against online opponents, that is a very rare feature ever seen among games and it's a very big plus, why? because then you don't have to ♥♥♥♥♥ your friends to get this game to play it together.
The controls are simple but the tactics are a little more complicated,  there is a lot you can do with the items you have it all depends on your current surrounding and what you make of it meaning that in the end the winner is determined by sheer skill and the ability to use his surroundings to his advantage rather than having op items or an op character, all characters are the exact same the only difference are the sounds/sprites/animations, the rest is the exact same which makes the game fair.
you can download workshop levels and play them with your friends or online, or if you prefer, you can make a level yourself and put it out there for others to enjoy.
Aside from all that there are also many easter eggs, there are at least 8 different secret characters that are unlockable via passwords in chat boxes (look it up) such as the goat from goat simulator, the guy from QWOP (just the fact that they decided to add this guy is hilarious) the characters from payday, gang beasts and of course, a potato.
there is a fair leveling system that has been added recently, every guy who finished the race before you, takes a few of your points away but every guy who finished behind you gives you a couple of points, all in all, you gain more points than lose so the system isn't unforgiving of mistakes.
your collective points decide which level you are and you are placed into races with players of matching ranks (of course you can choose to switch that option off but that's your funeral)
The game itself weighs very little and doesn't have high system requirements compared to some other game out there so it's light and easy to just pick up and play.
Of course the game does have a story mode that tests your skills in all sorts of situations but I don't want to spoil the story for you.
The game costs a bit but for what it's worth, it most certainly pays off quickly.
One last thing, this game is very competitive keep that in mind when inviting one of those friends who get mad or rage easily at stuff, you might have a bad time with them.

In the time before the oceans drank Atlantis,
There was an age Undreamed of...
Let me tell you of the days of High Adventure!!
With a 10 hour adjustment/settings period I began to seriously play my first 'Survival' genre title, and it's Conan, by Crom!
Great stuff here and very immersive. This is an alpha build at present, and you are very much paying a price to essentially playtest the game.  Funcom are fine developers and are addressing patches once, if not twice, daily -- and even working through the weekends.
Crafting is bugged, and lag is a permanent issue though constantly improving.
In my first two days my camp was assaulted thrice and defended once -- and the raiders only managed to do any real damage after breaking down my door and assassinating me in my sleep.  Good times.
THE GOOD:
Sword and sorcery adventure in a brutl survival setting where you must fight, scrouge, hunt, and craft to survive not only the hostilities of the exile wastelands, but other exiles like yourself who may be marauding for your head on the end of their blade.
THE BAD:
Bugged crafting and rubberbanding lag.  Performance varies widely between servers and population densities.  Game is in serious need of optimization -- and that's why you pay-to-play the Early Access. Ten minute-or-more load times are not uncommon.
After the first day Funcom fired PingPerfect for disasterous support on launch, and their 'official' servers only run under a 3rd party anti-cheat umbrella.  Opting out of installing 3rd party monitor-ware religates you to the thousands of homebrew servers, and that's not necessarily a bad thing.
THE UGLY:
People can be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s and it's sad to come back into the game to find yourself dead and 8 hours of crafting, building, designing, and grinding burned to the ground -- but that's the brutality of the Hyborian Age!
Also, drowning to death because lag places you on land when the server clearly left you in the middle of a lake isn't pleasant.  This game is not for the faint-of-heart or people who throw tantrums when things aren't butter-smooth out the box.
PRO-TIPS:
- When modifying controls in-game, it bugs out -- mouse speed, invert mouse, etc, do not work properly after an options change.  Remedy this by setting those options differently, selecting 'Apply', then settign them back to your desired specs and hitting 'Apply' again.
- You can hack up dead bodies for additional loot drops like hide and bone.
- Consolidate the 'duplicate items' crafting bug by dropping all of them into a single loot bag.
- Remedy the 'unuseable workbench' bug -- without having to re-log -- by modifying the totals of the ingredients use to craft the previous item.
- For best crafting results, use the exact number of ingredients per item, and select "Craft x".  Then the workbench will un-bug over time.
BOTTOM LINE:
'What is best in life?'
"To crush your enemies.
See them driven before you.
And to hear the lamentation of their women."

What can I say that hasn't already been said, Valkyria Chronicals is simply an amazing game. For me it was the first time encountering a game using a combination of active movement and turn based combat. In comparison to a game like Final Fantasy and other such turn based rpgs this game stands in a unique light, and unfortunately one of very few games that makes an attempt to use such a game play style. Overall the Music and sound design is superb, it does a excellent job of displaying the emotional value of a scene or making the moment more intense and thrilling for the player. The use of a book/journal to display chapters and other content like character bios, world information locations/weapons etc is perfect and fits the esthetic of the game. With a roster of 50+ characters its near impossible to walk away without a dozen favorites whether it be aesthetically or personality wise.
Overall its the perfect game, especially for those like myself who enjoy some strategic thinking. Not to say the game is overly difficult, but the unique gameplay, meshing of anime/war and watercolor style visuals really gives players a fresh taste and leaves me certainly wanting more.
Highly recommended.

Answer 1: You can modify the server settings (tuning almost any aspect of the game) to fit your playstyle. These settings can be modified before launching a singleplayer or local server as well. There are also official Blitz servers for those who like more action in their survival.
Complaint 2: It's laggy as hell and/or rubber-banding!
Answer 2: My laptop is 5 years old. If I leave the settings at automatic, not only does it look quite nice, it still runs at 30+ FPS. If I tweak the settings to fit my hardware, it easily runs at 60+ FPS. This level of optimization is WELL ahead of similar titles... As for the rubber-banding, I'm not sure if I can answer that one. I'm running on a privately hosted server with plenty of power and my game play is as smooth as can be. Perhaps the official servers have yet to be tweaked to such perfection? Also, my home internet connection is 60Mbps/5Mbps. Might be a helping factor.
Complaint 3: Progress is too slow!
Answer 3: See Answer 1.
Complaint 4: This is a shell of a game!
Answer 4: I've built shelters and started cults, all in a single day. However, this is the one time where I will remind my readers that this is an Early Access title... For being EA, this game has an amazing amount of content to be explored. I set all my server settings to max so that I could zip through and learn all I could from the game, and I'm very impressed. For starting content, there's much more available compared to similar titles at this stage. There's currently 10 different shields alone for you to cower behind. Also, did I mention cults?
Complaint 5: Everything kills you! You die too fast!
Answer 5: Okay, so don't run head-on into something twice your size... I've been killed plenty of times, but then I learned, and I adapted. I was much more cautious, kept my eyes open, and learned what creatures I could handle and which ones would eat me for breakfast. Eventually, with better stats and equipment, I got braver and died to bigger baddies! IT'S A SURVIVAL GAME! Expect the challenge to be in surviving...
Complaint 6: The servers are unstable/down/failing/bad!
Answer 6: Okay, so, really? Every online game in the history of online games lauds themselves on how quickly they recovered from their server issues after release. This game has not been released. I'm shocked they even have official servers at this stage. Find a private server, one that's well-hosted and reliable, and all your issues will go away. I'll open mine to the public once the game releases.
Complaint 7: The combat is clunky and hard!
Answer 7: I actually enjoyed how terrible I was at combat in the beginning. I learned, I leveled up, I adjusted my stats, and I got the hang of it. The combat is a little on the slow side, but then I like that split-second extra to think or to catch a spear on my shield and bash in a skull. It can be very enjoyable once you become accustomed to it.
Complaint 8: The thralls are crap!
Answer 8: I said I wouldn't say anything about this title being EA again, so... ATTACK, MY SLAVES! MUAHAHAHAHAHAAAA!!!... Seriously, though. I love the idea, and the thralls honestly just need some tweaking and expansion to turn them into the equivalent of say... I don't know... dinosaurs or whatever?
Complaint 9: It's such a grind!
Answer 9: See Answers 1 & 3. In my experience, however, even without the settings set to blitz, I seem to acquire resources quite fast and easily.
Complaint 10: Everything bum-rushes you from miles away!
Answer 10: No. The ferals, yes. IF they see you, they will rush you from quite a ways away. They're easy to deal with though, even bare-handed. With a weapon? They're hilariously easy to slash through. Bast part of the game, IMO. Most deadly creatures, however, have a reasonable aggro distance and are easy to avoid if you're careful.
Complaint 11: I keep dying of thirst!
Answer 11: Drink water. The game literally GIVES you a water skin from the word go, if you stopped to smell the roses that is. This is a ridiculous feat compared to similar titles where you can guzzle sea water through your pores and it takes quite some time before you can craft any kind of water skin... I've yet to have water or food issues. I keep my water skin full and I nom on bugs.
Complaint 12: People keep using exploits to demolish my base while I'm offline!
Answer 12: I know of two exploits that let you get through solid walls. Those were fixed several updates ago. Issues are to be expected, and FunCom is fixing the game-breaking issues just as fast as people can find them. I call that a win at this stage of the game. The main contributor to demolished bases is either A) you built a bad base or B) they nuked (used an avatar on) you. Issue A can be fixed by getting good and issue B can be fixed by joining a server that regulates avatars (see Answer 1).
Complaint 13: I keep getting killed while offline!
Answer 13: I know I keep saying it, but see Answer 1. Join a server that has offline killing disabled, or make one. I quite enjoy the realism as it drives me to protect my base better when all my friends are sleeping inside it.
Complaint 14: It takes too long to load!
Answer 14: Compared to similar titles, this game loads rediculously fast. How they optimized loading speeds to such a degree I can only attribute to prior experience in networked game programming via The Secret World. While on the other hand, I can only attribute slow load times to A) picking a slow server (in which case, pick another), B) having a crap-tastic garage rig of a computer, or C) having a crap-tastic connection speed. Even on 15Mbps-d/3Mbps-u (which is the slowest connection I have access to) I have no trouble with loading of any kind.
To be continued.

It's no Shovel Knight, and it's PAINFULLY short for the asking price (7 Hours on my end, and I wasn't trying to speed run), but Owlboy tries, and more-or-less succeeds to overcome it's short-commings and gutted story with sheer love and dedication. But buyer beware; if the game's art style doesn't charm you immediately, you're in for an expensive diversion.
Long Form: Keeping with the trend of 2016 video games, Owlboy's conclusion will leave a lot to be desired. The game plays well, though it's occasional obsession with having you navigate blind through pitch-black spike trap room is just bafflingly poor design. The game was in development hell, and it clearly shows, both in the bizzare pacing (The Primary Antagonist is never fought, despite having all of the spritwork done for an actual battle, there's an upgrade for a weapon that, by the time you can afford it, will only be useable once) and in an almost pointedly avoided Three-Magic-Items quest that seems to be happening for the villians more than for you.
But Owlboy is a light game, with a surprisingly heavy asking price. It's conclusion does not leave a good taste in the mouth, and there's precious little to recommend beyond the eye candy and the lovingly realised characters who, if not exactly genre defining, are at least fun and inoffensive.
Owlboy is inoffensive, which is the best I can say for it. It digests easily, passes quickly, and will be forgotten about within minutes of completing it. Let's hope 2017 shows us some games with actual, realised endings.

Apparantly I haven't made a review yet, so here goes.
Warframe is about a bunch of cool space ninjas running around space being vigilantes mass-murdering hordes of enemies and grinding bosses so that you can get even more space ninjas to add to your arsenal.
Personally speaking, I'd recommend this as the best F2P game on steam (Even better than TF2), due to the fact that you can obtain about 90~% of the items in the game at absolutely no cost. Although it does have a steep-ish learning curve due to the fact that there is little to no handholding in this game, once you go past that curve you can go solo everything with no problem, no trouble.
It's fun, it's fast-paced, and there's a little bit of everything for everyone, including what weapons you'd like, what colors you'd choose, what capes you'd wear, how you'd decorate your dojo, cats, dogs or sentinels.
The community isn't particularly toxic, and is extremely helpful most of the time, meaning that they'll be happy to hold your hand as you go along.
All in all, I'm happy with all the time I've spent in this game, and I don't regret spending money on the game to support the brilliant devs behind this fairly well designed game.

This is a 1920's mystery game set around a small American town and a group of 4 rebellious young high school girls. The gameplay is based around 4 minigames, at which winning or losing has consequences for the story and conversations you encounter. The story begins simply, but soon after branches off into multiple concurrent threads that all weave into a massive conspiracy controlling the town. You will do things like investigate a series of accidents involving shoddy mail-order products, try to get a talking horse elected mayor, and play cards with a ghost. By the end, the story has dropped most of its silly elements and a kind of horror borne of only slightly exaggerated early-20th century morality begins to make itself evident, and you have the choice of accepting it or rebelling. While I wouldn't call it a very ambiguous moral choice, it does provide alternate endings and interesting conversations.
Gameplay wise, it got a bit boring after a while, and there was very little consequences to losing at minigames because you could save before encounters and reload saves if you failed. The minigames are fine, but winning at them always had a level of randomness to it that make replaying segments you lost, where there were multiple minigames in a row you couldn't save in between, kind of frustrating. There is a sort of RPG aspect here, where the girls have stats that apply to different minigames and they could be leveled up with repeated playing of the minigames. However, no matter how high my stats got, I never felt significantly advantaged when it came to the minigames, above what I would normally have had just from knowing how to play them well.
The things that kept me playing were the storylines and the charming personalities of the characters. I legitimately wanted my girls to succeed in their adventures and was concerned for them when they got in trouble or were in danger. If this were a pure point and click adventure, or even a visual novel, and minimized or lessened the minigame elements in favor of using and levelling the stats in a different way, I felt I would have enjoyed the game even more, but for what it is I had fun and will play it again one day. I give this title a solid 7/10, a great effort from this developer with a really unique storytelling style.

One of the few games these days that are just plain fun to play with other people.
First of all, it had local coop, but to my surprise I had discovered that you can play local coop as well as online coop simultaneously, that is, you and your friends can play together on one screen whilst going up against online opponents, that is a very rare feature ever seen among games and it's a very big plus, why? because then you don't have to ♥♥♥♥♥ your friends to get this game to play it together.
The controls are simple but the tactics are a little more complicated,  there is a lot you can do with the items you have it all depends on your current surrounding and what you make of it meaning that in the end the winner is determined by sheer skill and the ability to use his surroundings to his advantage rather than having op items or an op character, all characters are the exact same the only difference are the sounds/sprites/animations, the rest is the exact same which makes the game fair.
you can download workshop levels and play them with your friends or online, or if you prefer, you can make a level yourself and put it out there for others to enjoy.
Aside from all that there are also many easter eggs, there are at least 8 different secret characters that are unlockable via passwords in chat boxes (look it up) such as the goat from goat simulator, the guy from QWOP (just the fact that they decided to add this guy is hilarious) the characters from payday, gang beasts and of course, a potato.
there is a fair leveling system that has been added recently, every guy who finished the race before you, takes a few of your points away but every guy who finished behind you gives you a couple of points, all in all, you gain more points than lose so the system isn't unforgiving of mistakes.
your collective points decide which level you are and you are placed into races with players of matching ranks (of course you can choose to switch that option off but that's your funeral)
The game itself weighs very little and doesn't have high system requirements compared to some other game out there so it's light and easy to just pick up and play.
Of course the game does have a story mode that tests your skills in all sorts of situations but I don't want to spoil the story for you.
The game costs a bit but for what it's worth, it most certainly pays off quickly.
One last thing, this game is very competitive keep that in mind when inviting one of those friends who get mad or rage easily at stuff, you might have a bad time with them.

Part board game, part card game, part RPG and part action game. Create two sets of cards. One set is of items to find. The other set is of encounters. Thankfully the NPC (game master?) shuffles and sorts everything out for you.
The GM places cards on the table in various configurations and you move a taoken along the cards as you would on a grid or board. Sometimes you have more than one direction from which to choose. Most often you can only more in one direction. Once chosen you reveal the card to see what you encounter. You may encounter combat, find equipment, make a choice as to your action or many others. Don't forget to stock up on food as each card your token moves to will cost one food.
After traveling awhile (down stairs to new 'floors'), you find the end boss. Use your equipment to defeat this foe the same way you beat any previous combat. Use the ASWD keys to swing your current weapon. Other items may give you other skills and will be explained as you get them. If you beat the boss, you'll unlock many new cards and can change your decks around to include them if you wish.
Tailor your decks to what you think might happen. Add more armor, a shield or even stronger weapons. There is a lot you cannot plan for, so I suggest erring on the side of caution.
You can always go into another 'dungeon' to fight a boss you have already fought. To start a game, choose the boss you want to fight then choose the difficulty for what is needed to unlock specials. No spoiler given here.
Good luck and no matter what the GM says, don't turn back

Ah Warframe. For the past 3 weeks this is all i have played, it is a free 2 play game done correctly. Story is odd at first but gets good later on and drags you into it with good twists and great cinimatics with a BEAUTIFUL soundtrack. Gameplay is fun, grindy, but you dont really mind the grind to much. Warframes feel unique and fun to use, and weapons do as well. This game makes you feel like a total badass, being able to wall run while shootng, doing flips, sliding on ziplines, it feels like so much fun. This game also caters to every playstle and i GUERENTEE there is a warframe for you out there. If you want to full stealth a map you can, if you want to set off every alarm, you can do that. Meele combat doesnt feel like a stale spam fest, it feels like that at the start, but once you learn how to use stance cards, it feels like something like for honor or a good fighting game, the combos feel fluid and look good. The wide selection of weapons and frames is great, but even grater is the coustemization you can do in this game. This game is nick named "fashionframe" and i can see why. There are coupious amount of colors, helmets, skins, effects, and even followers you can change. I digress though. Warframe is an amazing game, with fun fast paced action, or slow stealthy action if you want. It is a great game done right.

Well, i don't like to write bad reviews, but new people should be advised about this game.
Regarding the Pros and Cons:
Pros:
+ Zombie addiction: i think it's the most beautiful thing in a rts game: with big battle you can turn the field in a bloody horde of zombie that will go to attack your base and everything they will meet, you need to burn them or send your civilians for cleaning the bodies or the zombies will spawn every time.

+ Mod kit is coming for early july
Cons:
- Lag: there is lag when you play with more than 1 AI or versus other players. This is a bad thing in the game, it ruins a lot your game's exprience.
- The map variety is not so good. All the map are similar, and they need a re-balance for the resources nodes.
- Ai: Despite the last improvements, it still needs a lot of work.
Conclusion:
Devs are trying hard for improving the game, but they are a small company, so it needs long time before having a 'full and complete game'.

My initial impression of Warframe was that someone had made a huge mistake, and I'd received a rather expensive game for free. As it turns out, Warframe IS free. Which is incredible considering the polished graphics, and quality as it's presented.
Don't be fooled; Warframe is definitely a time sink. Levelling up a Warframe to use better weapons, to then level them further and unlock better mods for weapons - this cycle continues. There is a serious lack of content aside from the same set of missions. 'Smash 'em up carnage and mindless fun' is a great way to describe the game.
- A huge pull, Warframes, weapons, and ships are
customisable, and the sheer number of each available is insane. While there are real cash transactions, almost everything in the game can be crafted with some effort on your part, barring cosmetic skins/items. I do feel a little miffed that most colour palletes are also locked behind this paywall. I'm not PSYCHED to be a Red Power Ranger, but guess I will be one unless this changes.
- Saying this, the atmosphere and graphics are excellent. It plays and looks fantastic on my GTX1070, with the camera at a third person view, and OTS zooms for scoped or long-range weapons.
- Combat feels seamless in singleplayer, I have had no problems except for my own inadequacy with a gun (which is slowly improving.) With multiplayer, I have noticed a significant amount of movement lag.
- If you're used to being a long-term clicker, like me, your fingers are probably going to ache after CTRL+ SPACE/SHIFT jumping combos (but you do look hella cool.)
There is a LOT of focus on co-op play, and if you suffer from anxiety as I do, I would suggest playing with friends only or changing settings for solo missions. Unfortunately, my experience of the public community is that it is quite a toxic one. Others may not feel this is the case, but for the majority of the time I've played and spent in public groups, there is a ton of verbal abuse over voice chat/nasty trolls, and as a new player it is -hugely- off-putting.  I have learned of the mute option since, but it feels that the longer a game is released, especially of the MMO variety, and the larger player base it gains, the worse the community gets. [Cue group rushed playthroughs, abuse, stress, panic attacks and not wanting to play again for extended periods of time on my part.]
I await the day a majority friendly community lasts in any MMO, but I may as well live in hope of Half-Life 3.
*As to the new Plains of Eidolon update; oh man, THE GRIND IS REAL. It feels as though the developers tried to create a rolling, open world landscape for players to explore and complete missions at their leisure, but the missions are really just repetitive bounties that you have to run all the way back and extract to the main hub to complete. That doesn't fit well with an open world setting.
Repeatable quests and bounties which are required for reputation gain
Feeling forced to grind them for rewards and necessary mats after a relatively 'do whatever you feel kind of vibe,' is odd. It would work well as an increment to a large update, but as the update itself, it feels rather shallow.*

Conan exiles, after 10 or so hours of gameplay, is a great game despite many issues in it. The good thing about the issues in this game especialy for early acess is that they are things that the devs have actively said they are working on or things that i know from game dev experience can be solved. One thing that has made me want to stick with this game through its development its the developers want and ability to keep the game up to date, they have worked hard on already releasing 3 or 4 patches of decent size within 4 days of games release and they all seem to fix issues, well for me they do.
This game has a great concept and is executed fairly well for the stage its in. yes there are issues, but the game istelf works well, its playable, it has some good concepts that work well and some that dont, but that is why they are in early acess, to actively find out what works and what doesnt with the community that play it.
Now for a list of pros and cons
Pros:
Graphics and optimisation-
The Graphics on this game are good, they seem polished at this stage and i think most importantly it runs well. for me other ea games like this run poorley barely getting 30 fps (I have a terrible computer) but this game gives me at least 40 most of the time.
The game world-
The game world is really well done, i love the setting and the feel, not much more to say about it really, exploraion is great and I love the animals and buildings etc.
Cons:
Current Lag issue-
There has been a lag issue on almast all servers i have found from day 1, Bad news is, it is the one thing really holding thus game back currently, good news is they are actively working on this to fix it so i hope to see it out of the cons list soon.
The games leveling and UI for that
Yes, the game i feel does have an issue with leveling, i found thati spend most of mmy points eraly on into some blacksmithing so light armour and light weapons, only to have found out that now i wont be able to go down the building path completely due to using quite a few points up. i think there are some big improvements that can be done here but ill leave them for another time. The Leveling ui definately needs a think over, they are all out of order, there is no "tree" as such just making it hard and confusing on what you want to do and need.
Combat
The combat currently feels odd, it may just be the server lag but some eneies feel way to weak and some too strong, and the way it works doesnt add for much skill just click fast.
So everything i have said good or bad about this game may be a different experience for othe people, bit as of right now this is a good early acess game with developers who seem to know wha they are doing

I will preface this review by saying that Owlboy is, overall, a good game that most people will enjoy. Looking at it objectively, it is at least a solid 6 or 7 out of 10. Those who value art and are able to get into the story are likely to rate it even higher. This review, however, is here to express the viewpoint of someone who did not particularly enjoy most of the game, and to explain why it might be one to avoid for similarly minded gamers.
In a nutshell, there is one thing Owlboy does amazingly, one thing it does atrociously, and a lot of perfectly adequate game in the middle. The pixel art is second to none. The game's lengthy development cycle is evident in every single piece of scenery, every character, every cutscene, and most importantly every gorgeous animation. The artists that worked on this game deserve nothing but praise, as they have managed to achieve something truly beautiful. I have seen a number of people compare this game to Ori and the Blind Forest, and in the art department that comparison is certainly an apt one. Ori may still be the king of gaming visuals overall, but Owlboy steals the crown when it comes to pixel art.
Where Owlboy does not compare favourably to something like Ori is in the gameplay, and here comes my greatest nitpick. I say nitpick, because for many people this will likely be much less of a problem than it was for me. If you're a gamer who shares this particular niggle, however, you'll understand immediately how one seemingly small problem can all but ruin an otherwise enjoyable experience:
I am not at all exaggerating when I say that I never once played Owlboy for longer than five minutes without the game wresting control away from me. Most of the time the interruptions were far more frequent.
Whether it is for a character to deliver a line of dialogue, a cutscene to occur, a door to open, or some other scripted event to play out, Owlboy delights in dragging you out of the moment with constant jarring interruptions that destroy the pacing and flow of the experience. The vast majority of these are completely unnecessary. Even many of the lines of dialogue do not require a pause in the gameplay for them to be delivered. There are moments in the game where characters talk, doors open, and scripted sequences occur *without* taking control away from the player, and they all work perfectly.
The most egregious examples of the above are when otherwise intense boss fights are interrupted multiple times for lines of completely unnecessary dialogue to be delivered and phase transitions to occur. I cannot stress enough just how much of a toll this takes on the pacing of the gameplay. Intense moments fall flat, brain-tickling puzzles become annoying, and any section you have to repeat more than once becomes infinitely more tiresome thanks to the arbitrary interruptions. This problem permeates every aspect of Owlboy, dragging the entire experience down and souring a lot of the game's goodness. It's such a shame to see, especially after such a long development cycle, because all of it would have been completely avoidable with more awareness of how to create good pacing in gameplay.
Besides the above, most of Owlboy falls into solid "good" territory. There are annoyances here and there, but also plenty of cool moments and clever bits of design to counterbalance them. There's no map or objective indicator, which can at times be a frustration in a metroidvania-esque game like this, but for the most part the levels are elegant and direct enough to avoid too much confusion. The bosses are very fun and satisfying when they aren't interrupted too much, and all of them are unique and memorable. The story is just fine, though nothing to write home about. There's enough emotion and drama to hit plenty of people right in the feels, but in a world where we have games like Undertale or The Walking Dead, the writing ultimately comes across as pretty middle of the road. There's passion and heart in it, however, and while the dramatic beats didn't really have enough substance for me, Owlboy at least puts far more effort into its story than the majority of games out there. The soundtrack similarly hits the correct emotional beats, but none of the tracks ever stuck in my mind for long or made me want to look them up on youtube afterwards.
Core gameplay-wise, again, it's just fine. Shooting is fun and punchy. The dash feels good. General movement is okay, but doesn't have much satisfying momentum or weight to it. You don't soar like a bird so much as just drift around the screen. There are a couple of ill-considered platforming segments that do not feel good to play at all, but they're few and far between. Some abilities and their associated controls feel responsive and well-implemented, others are a little finicky. Most of the game's puzzle gimmicks are enjoyable if a little shallow. There's really not a whole lot to talk about in this regard. Owlboy plays just fine. It does what it needs to do. Not great, not bad, just good enough and largely competent.
In regards to difficulty, Owlboy is quite forgiving without ever feeling too easy. There's just enough challenge to make beating bosses and clearing areas satisfying. Some bits will be tough for players who are less experienced with the genre, but it's by no means a hardcore game. It hits the middle of the spectrum incredibly well.
In summary, I was someone who hoped Owlboy might be a real game of the year candidate for me, in much the same way Ori and the Blind Forest was. Unfortunately, while Owlboy looks every bit the part, it doesn't quite stand up in the gameplay department. The constant interruptions were an ever-present problem, and everything else, while consistently above-average, rarely wowed me in the same way similar titles have. I made sure to finish the game so as to piece together an informed opinion on it, but at times it was something of a slog.
If you're not picky about interruptions to gameplay, Owlboy is almost certainly worth the buy. There's a lot of great stuff in there, and if you love good art then it's worth the price tag for that alone. If you're a fan of the gameplay in titles like Ori and the Blind Forest, Shovel Knight or Freedom Planet, however (and if you're keenly aware of *why* their gameplay works so well), Owlboy may be something of a disappointment.

Good game, would be better if there was full controller support. As it stands now, only half of the menus and actions have button icons to help you figure out how to navigate, and the mouse cursor keeps jumping onto the middle of the screen despite using a controller for this game.
NOTE: There is an issue with the game engine. If you make any kind of custom setting in the video settings a lot of effects like normal maps, shadows, bloom, etc. will be disabled. You must only select a preset within the game. After that you can edit the config file located in "~\%user name%\Documents\Steam Cloud\%steam name%\DreadOut\cloud\20140722011532\profile.cfg".
I recommend two additonal performance enhancements. This game takes a huge fps hit with the game's built-in antialiasing. Use antialiasing in your driver control panel instead. The Steam overlay also hurts the fps quite a bit too in this particular game, and will even run a modern video card (GTX 660) very hot with it enabled.
What I did was use the game preset of Fantastic (highest preset), exit the game, set the aa to 0 in the .cfg file, disable Steam overlay on this title, forced aa in the driver control panel, and now it's a steady 60 fps and looks great.

Kingdom Wars 2: Battles is a RTS with an interesting crafting system entwined with classic RTS gameplay and a great story.
The Story:
The story in Kingdom Wars 2: Battles is a great one pitting Humans against Orcs from the get go. The cutscenes are narrated with quality dialog making it feel like you are there commanding the forces and overcoming the challenges. The setting is somewhat different from other RTS games due to Human forces being on the defensive from the invading Orcs. To avoid any large spoilers I won’t go further into detail  but it is a story that will keep you playing.
Gameplay:
Now gameplay is where any RTS shines the most. There are several ways to overcome a challenge like instead of scaling walls with ladders why not smash it in with a battering ram! There are plenty of units to complement anyone's play style. The crafting aspects enhance the gameplay further giving you an edge over your enemy.In today’s internet age no game is complete without multiplayer. Kingdom Wars 2: Battles has your multiplayer RTS needs covered with intense PVP or co-operative play. There are also free content updates no season pass to get the latest chapter or added content! So many great things but every game has some bad mixed in with the good. The tutorial could have been longer and more in depth on certain mechanics. Resource management takes some getting used to. Overall it was still one of the best gameplay experiences in months for me
Bugs and Glitches:
No game is perfect bugs and glitches happen they are fixed Kingdom Wars 2: Battles has only a few annoying bugs. One cutscene bugged forcing me to close the game.There are some visual bugs also like textures stretching in weird ways. The bugs and glitches are mostly minor and don’t lessen the gameplay or story quality at all.
Pros and Cons:
Pros:
Great story
Crafting system
Card battles
Intense battles
Multiplayer
Multiple unit types
Voiced dialog
Help menu
Multiple ways to overcome a challenge
Free expansion pack
Cons:
Small visual bugs
Tutorial could be better
Resource management can be tough for those new to the game

Elsword is a whole lot of fun if you're into fighting games. The game has an interesting cast of characters and very, very many choices regarding movesets and playstyle. The game's  skills system is expansive and sometimes seems too big, but I'm an indecisive person, so I just had to deal with it. The core game mechanics are wonderful, and the ability to chain combos off of one another almost flawlessly is incredibly gratifying.
The equipable weapon and armor system is interesting, but it can get very annoying to micromanage and the sheer amount of items and numbers to consider can be a turnoff.
One major complaint I have is that the game seems to be centered around these events that keep you playing. The game will give you the opportunity to find these crazy items and equipable armor or weapons, which is awesome and all, but you can lag behind a lot if you miss an event. In short, the game struggles heavily with power creep- they keep ramping up the power of these exclusive weapons and items so that you can be even stronger if you get the stuff from this event, and the cycle continues as the stats go higher.
Also, the item drops can get flat out ridiculous. For instance, on my main character I accumulated over 1200 Complete Recovery Potions. Those things restore all your hp and mp! What the hell?! This basically makes me unkillable in any dungeon of my level, which makes the game cool for a little bit but boring and trudging after a while.
Overall though, I'd recommend it.

Have you wondered what it would be like to run a shop as an anime girl in a Japanese RPG? If so, then Recettear: An Item Shop’s Tale is what you’ve so desired. And it IS an indie game, which again shows that, as usual, the AAA games industry can’t be counted on to touch the part of us which wants to play as a pretty little girl.
One of this game’s taglines is “Capitalism, ho!” Recette, the protagonist and girl, says it with a big smile, and her eyes closed. Or maybe that’s how I remember her. With her open, maroon vest, green tie, belt buckle, and those two, large, red beads, maintaining strands of her caramel-colored hair in a tail beside her head. Plus that mortified facial expression of hers, whenever she hears opinions disparaging her business. She is so young.
The game, though. There’s more to it than those tan sleeves, over arms which she keeps parallel to her sides, with her palms wide open, giving the appearance of an angel. There is, indeed, more to the game. For example: does she live alone? Sort of. She lives with a fairy. Her mother seems to have passed away. And as for her dad, he seems to have abandoned her, and with lots of debt. You must be the godlike father she evidently never had. You must take possession of her body and ensure she pays off her dad’s debt so as to avoid being dispossessed of everything except, perhaps, her clothes.
Alas, that form of losing leads to one of the game’s weak points. For if you do lose (if you can’t pay your in-game debtors), you start from the “beginning,” with many of the advantages you’ve accrued in your defunct playthrough. This has you suffer what was already an uninspired dungeon crawler even more, as you’re sort of playing it all over again. It is by this and other means that you get to see little Recette running around, pit pat pit pat. By these you get to see her buy valuable items at low prices and sell them at high prices. You get to watch her go to sleep and awake, and reveal her innermost thoughts to her fairy friend. And it is all well-written, well-drawn, and….

FIRST IMPRESSIONS REVIEW:
*I'm writing this review from the stance of a complete beginner, trying to explain how it feels to be a newcomer. I'm sure not all of what I say rings true for every player, however I just wanted to put this out there for anyone looking to join the community as of late 2017. I hope all veterans can appreciate that. Cheers!*
At the time of writing this review, I only have around 3.5 hours on Warframe, however I felt as though there would be no better way to encapsulate my first impressions than to write a review after just beginning my journey. As the status quo for reviews goes, here is my list of pro's and con's.
Pro's:
+ Fluid gameplay (very satisfying and easy to understand game mechanics)
+ Graphically pleasing (While not at the cutting edge, the graphics do much more than an adequate job of engrossing me in the world of Warframe)
+ Unique (While not the first of its kind, the game somehow maintains a refreshing element from the rinse and repeat TPS  games currently out there)
+ Player base (currently one of the most played games on Steam, have yet to not find a squad)
+ Free-to-play! (Seemingly hundreds of hours of gameplay with no other costs than your electric bill)
+ Depth (This, for me, is a double edge sword, but after playing for few hours, I fel as though I've only scratched the surface of the content within this game)
+ Community (Have yet to encounter a toxic player, everyone thus far has been friendly and helpful)
Con's:
+ Depth (While I did add this to the pro's list as well, the game's sheer volume can be a bit overwhelming for a newcomer)
+ Microtransactions (Definitely not game-breaking as far as I know, however I personally believe microtransactions should be purely cosmetic)
+ Learning curve (The game seems to have an economy of its own, that was created by the players. I'm sure as time goes by I will get the hang of it, however this seems a little complex to a complete beginner. I'd like to add that the wiki, as well as YouTube videos, have been a big help thus far.
All in all, I'm very much enjoying Warframe thus far, and can certainly see myself playing this game for a good, long, time. The graphics, game mechanics, depth, lore, and immersive gameplay pull together to create a truly unique, refreshing experience, that you have no reason to not at least try for yourself. Now it's time to force my friends to download it!

15 hours in and I think its about time to give an initial impression review.
Some info first. I currently play single player, I may move into a PVE server in a month or so, giving the Devs time to fix some of their current server issues. PVP is not for me so their will be no mention of it here.
I'm also a patient man and understand its an EA game and not finished - Very important!
Ok, the game. You will find a bit more depth below but so far I am thoroughly enjoying it, its similar enough in playstyle to other games I have liked (Ark) to make it easy enough to get into.
Upon selecting Single player/ Co op mode your presented with a host of server options allowing me to tailor my game to suit me, which is a good addition albeit it may require a bit of adjustment to learn which way to move certain slider options ( The tooltip gives info on what the option does, and some are obvious as to which way to move the slider, others may not be, however you can adjust them in game) After a while I found the default settings for xp (especially crafting xp) and harvesting to be a little on the low side so adjusted them up to suit my style.
Next is character selection which provides the usual customisation options.
Then its name your character, see what he/she has been exiled for and you are into the game.
Immediately into game and there is no tutorial, you are pretty much on your own, thankfully if you have played other similar genre games you will quickly pick up what you need to do.
Heading north I came across my first enemy, well, he came to me, aggro range in this game if pretty far, so if the enemy is facing you and you can see him, chances are he will see you and come for you. Once it was dispatched, I seen some NPCS at a camp fire. They seen me, and after running like hell, I ran out of stamina, they caught me and I died. Enemys will pursue you a lot further than most games I've played.
I also noticed that NPCs/Creatures seem to lag at distance, but closer they get the better it becomes. I have no doubt this will be fixed in time.
At lower levels the game can be tough, you will soon learn what you can handle and what to avoid. Essentially the further north you venture the harder it becomes.
The building aspect pretty far is as I expect with a reasonable amount of structures to unlock as you level. Although once past the intial stone stage you will have to travel into more dangerous territory for iron etc, which I guess is as it should be.
I have only come across 2 bugs, one of which was a crash to desktop (clicking on food to eat it while it is still in a storage box, instead of moving it to inventory first) The other was arrow stacks in your inventory dropping to 1 arrow when logging back into game (I place my arrows in a box before logging out now and besides, they are not hard to replace) Again, I have no doubt these will be fixed in time.
Combat is simple and as I expect and like it, ie you swing, you hit or if you have a shield you block. I know others expected more, but its good for me.
One thing to note is that I think item durability is currently too low, ie things break too fast. So expect to repair items a lot! I'm hoping this is addressed in time.
I dont see any performance issues, the game looks good, there is certainly plenty to do so far. Things are pretty much as I expected a game of this genre to be and with time can only get better.

Owlboy is an evolution of what the 16-bit era could have turned into if the Sony Playstation had never come along and we had somehow gotten a Super Nintendo 2. It's one of the prettiest pixel art games out there, filled with dashes of Zelda, Chrono Trigger and Rocket Knight Adventures.
It's also imperfect. The game spent 9 years in gestation, and it shows. Portions of the game's plot seem muddy, as if there were too many cooks in the kitchen, and the ending is one of the strangest, most ambiguous things I've seen in a while. (It's very Final Fantasy VII - people who played that will know what I mean.) On a technical level, it seems that crafting all of that lovely pixel art took a priority over level design, which is fairly pedestrian, and there's one mini-game involving a cannon that crosses the line from challenging to unfun.
Despite this, I cannot help but recommend Owlboy to everyone who guided Link through the Lost Woods to find the Master Sword as a child. It has a certain amount of sparkling magic to it that only small teams working on passion projects can create, and even if it doesn't quite hit the same heights as its inspiration, it's still worth experiencing - if only to get a tingle of that 16-bit era of adventure once again.

text: A gorgeous charming game. I don't often review games, but this one seemed to warrant it.

Ronan is a criminal-turned-cop who is killed by the mysterious Bell Killer. Playing as Ronan's ghost, investigate a series of crime scenes (sometimes with the help of teenage medium Joy), searching for identity of the killer. Many supernatural elements come into play – ghosts, witches, demons – and some flashbacks of the witch trials are pretty gruesome (drowning, burning, hanging).
As the investigation progresses, you'll explore a graveyard, an apartment house, an old mansion, a police station and of course the obligatory asylum level. While the game world is small, it is open, with the ability to just wander around the town of Salem. It's a gloomy place – the game occurs entirely at night – but is well-dotted with NPCs and collectibles. Obtaining collectibles can unlock other stories (usually brief, narrated cut-scenes), and some NPCs will provide side-missions. There's a decent amount of stuff to do, but most collectibles were easily found as I explored the town or a level.
Investigations require exploring a a crime scene, finding evidence (“Press E to analyze”) and sorting through the collected evidence (“Press Q to conclude the investigation”). Walking (or later, teleporting) around as a ghost feels fun; Ronan can walk through walls, possess people (mind-reading), and turn on random stuff to mess with the townsfolk (poltergeisting). Especially cool were the impenetrable “ghost walls” from past times that can block Ronan from exploring – or even provide new hazards (watch out for the ghost train!). Oh, and you can possess cats, too. This is actually crucial to progress through several stages of the game.
The demon sections, though, dragged the experience down a bit. Demons will sometimes spawn after completing an investigation. Their existence does have a crucial part to play, and they're easy enough to defeat with a little patience. Given that this is a supernatural tale, it would be rather weird if demons of some kind weren't in the game, and having some stealth sections added some variety to the gameplay. But after a while the demons became annoying distractions from the story.
And the narrative is where Murdered: Soul Suspect stands strongest. There is a lot of backstory to be found about Ronan and his wife (via collectibles). Sometimes collectibles are merely annoying, but they are worth pursuing here. Jason Brooks (as Ronan) and Cassidy Lehrman (as the medium, Joy) provide stand-out vocal performances. The graphics (Unreal 3) are great – murky and dark. Jason Graves' score provides a classic horror-story undertone. Murdered: Soul Suspect is a well-crafted detective game with a few quirks that holds its story aloft as its best attribute. If that sounds good to you, then go ahead and get this one.

Only played it for 3+ hours, I've decided to write a review here.
For a developer that being funded by indie backer at indiegogo, I believe that they're living up my expectations.
Basically, what do you expect with funds only 29,000 USD? Being developed for a year, I believe those value didn't last long in the US. Calculate average salary per month for a programmer, they don't have enough money practically.
Therefore, I try give my not-so-called-objectives review, given those handicap.
Graphics : 7/10
Arguably their main weak point. Although unity engine that being used by them have more capability, they simply didn't have enough manpower to polish the graphic. The character details is just like PS2 or XBOX era. Character animation also is not very "amusing", but playable.
However, despite of the lack details in the character, they put much effort in surrounding details. Much of the details are handcrafted individually. They put effort to give Easter egg for their backer. Look for each poster and note, you'll find out that most of it are handcrafted. But you can feel that they use lighting and shadows to compromise with the lack of character details.
Gameplay: 9/10
For me, this is their main strong point. Remember Fatal Frame? Remember how the atmosphere they built in that? For me, Dreadout is giving the same, if not better, horror atmosphere than Fatal Frame. Try to play it in the middle of the night, with surround speakers and when you're alone ;)
Maybe this game is rather hard for person that is not a hardcore gamers. This is due to the developer didn't gave much information in-game. You need to figure out by yourself, what you need to do. It's a good point to draw you closer to heroine experience. However, there's a lot of guide out there to guide you out from your frustration :)
If you notice, the developer of this game give the opening cut-scene with "Lingsir Wengi" song. For locals like me, this is the song that "told" by many to draw evil spirit came. More than enough to give a goosebumps :(
The only minus in gameplay is it only last few hours. You want it more after finished it.
Music: 9/10
Another strong point of this game. The OST is good. Googling the artist list and review the OST, they worth to be downloaded :)
Final Verdict : 8.5/10
They put a good atmosphere to overcame the graphic limitation. And good soundtrack also. Actually, I want to give them 10/10 due to being handicapped in development budget. But, even with that handicap, they deserve a good rating from me :)

BOTS

Owlboy was in development for 10 + years, and has been hyped seemingly to no end since last year before it's eventual release.
So was the hype well placed? Well, let's see.
First, accessability.
I like that this game doesn't feel too large in file size, and yet isn't too small so that you're at least aware there's a decent amount of content, probably not for 25 dollars worth, but I guess that aspect is debatable.
First impressions : The Story / Visuals / Soundtracks / Gameplay
Story : Starts rather well, it seems to put the player at odds with the world which is a GREAT way to start a story in adventure games, yet it just falls short after you leave the first area. Reasons I'll explain in Gameplay.
Visuals : The pixel art, some dungeon settings, and the Boss Fights are all visually impressive for the game genre it's replicating, yet a lot of exploring the world of Owlboy will feel extremely mundane and repetitive, for reasons to explain in Gameplay, and mostly because the settings all look extremely similar and it's tiring to the eyes more then once.
Soundtrack / SFX : I liked one song from this entire game, and it was out of genorisity. Other then that, nothing to be too ecstatic for. I'd pick Ocarina of Time over this game for the soundtrack alone.
Gameplay (long section) : And now we get to the point where I start to wonder if video games are even video game anymore, because 90% of the appeal to this game is solely based in its atmosphere. Everything else about this game is tedium to the fifth power, and it ends up just feeling like a mediocre "Zelda-with-flying" borefest. Exploring the world of Owlboy almost penalizes the player because of how genuinely awful traveling from one place to the other is, and how goddamned slow the Bird moves in the air when you aren't rolling, and even the rolling just makes the fact that this game seems like a mediocre Zelda clone just makes the bore of this game sink in even further.
The world of Owlboy is creative, but it doesn't DO anything of value with it, and rather just makes the player have little incentive to explore it.
I WILL recommend this title, only because it has appeal to others, and IS a good way to start the platforming genre, but as someone who spends an unhealthy amount of time playing better platformers, this definitely isn't the best of that genre.
Tl;DR : Fork out the money for this game at your own risk / leisure. The presentation of the world of Owlboy does decent, but the gameplay makes it fade into irrelevance. Play this if you are NEW to platformers, and have never even touched Donkey Kong Country / OoT / Super Mario Sunshine / Mario 64.
I really enjoy narrative games and that's what this is. Almost no action at all, save for a handful of stealth sequences. It was like watching a 12 hour movie and I liked it.

ArcheAge is a mixed bag.
On one hand, it's a gorgeous game. Running on a modified CryEngine, it features fantastic character models, outfits, weapons and mounts. It's landscapes are as vast as they are detailed. The ability to set sail on it's massive, gorgeous seas adds a new layer to the already played out genre. Who doesn't fantasize about being a pirate?
Player owned plots are a throwback to days where MMO developers brought a balanced approach in delivering the goods to their playerbase. The community driven market is nothing new but very much welcomed.
At first sight, it really seems like ArcheAge has the potiential to redefine MMO's for the better.
!BUT!
Then we run into their atrocious P2W model. This game is a MMO whales wet dream. Sadly this applies to both the PvE and PvP aspect of the game.  As an examle, the taxation on player plots is rather high. Labour (which is required to craft, which is 1/2 the game in itself) is such a transparent cash grab that it's slightly infuriating. Then there is the fact that North American publisher 'Trion Worlds' is terrible at communicating with their community and when they do, they often renag on their word. Lest I mention their biased community support leads found in their forums.
Ultimately, at the end of the day, ArcheAge offers VERY little for seasoned veterans of the MMO landscape. However, for new comers to the genre it may very well be the game that gets them hooked. As somone who purchased a 'Founders Pack' which is the MOST I've ever single-handedly spend on a video game, turned out to be such a farce, I'm compelled to tell the average gamer to stay away. If you REALLY need to play an MMO, renew your WoW account.

DreadOut is a survival-horror game that focus heavily on puzzle solving, item hunting, and a few bosses fights if you meet the requirement items. Although graphic wise it isn't much to compare with other games with huge staff and budget, the mechanics are consistent enough and the dialogue and puzzles are decent.
Since the game mechanics mostly based on Fatal Frame (with a modern twist) it treated the player like a veteran Fatal Frame player, and the game don't hold your hand in anyway (though I recomended reading the How-to-Play at the tittle screen for beginners and veteran player either way)
The music in most cases are really well done, but a bit awkward in others. The animation of the NPCs are weird and clunky but you won't be bothered with it much since in the first act you won't be spending much time with them.
Ghost and Boss fights are well done in a lot of aspects. Some are straightforward big-scary-strong monster and some are one-shot at their weak spot. The game makes you question what strategy you should use at each ghost encounter. If you are defeated by a ghost, don't worry. The game won't punishes you harshly for your mistakes but instead sends you to a limbo stage for you to think what mistakes you have made.
At first sight, items you encountered may seems useless but if you gathered all of them, the buff, or power up, you get will eventually noticable. So, don't be afraid to explore!
The game does well to deliver an intense atmosphere once you entered the "Night-Stage" combining music ambience and ghost passing through hallways at moments where you are most restless hearing strange noises.
Although the first act was short (about 2-3 hours first playthrough), the second act is being develop to patch as future DLC (which cost absolutely nothing, don't worry)
In summary, if you are looking for a fresh horror without western influances, and willing to sacrifice next-gen graphic, this is the game for you which only cost 15$. But if you couldn't handle the low-budget looks of the game, I suggest otherwise. But either way, you will be missing out on experiencing a new asian horror if you choose to not play this.

I went in with a head full of high hopes.  Unfortunately, the few decent ideas this game has are ruined by completely miserable gameplay and design.  Expect bugs, enemies that will stunlock you to death, a system that punishes the player for dying by making them wait arbitrary, incrementally-increasing amounts of time to respawn, obtuse, illogical puzzles, poor voice acting and translation work, dated graphics, stiff, absurd character animation, directionless pixel hunting, paths that continue infinitely instead of dead-ending...
About that death system?  When your character dies, you get to engage in the delightful minigame of running in a straight line towards a respawn point.  The first time you die, the jog takes about 15 seconds.  With each death the run becomes longer and longer.  As soon as you die, the game autosaves and checkpoints you, so there's no way of avoiding this sequence.  By the time I quit out to write this review, I counted the tedious errand taking upwards of a minute.  The developers brag about this mechanic in the in-game manual.
I don't like this game.  It's a shame, because there's some genuinely cool imagery and a handful of good scares, but the experience of playing it is nothing but frustrating.  Put your money towards one of the many other more polished and enjoyable horror games on Steam.
